chapters.title: Chapter 1819: First Round - 1
paragraphs: The giant randomizer above the arena began to spin.

One hundred names appeared within the vast screen of light, each one glowing with a different intensity according to the participant’s aura, identity, and pillar mark. The names moved so quickly that most people could not follow them with their eyes. They circled, crossed, separated, and merged again like golden stars caught inside a heavenly wheel.
Angelina Valerius stood calmly above the central stage, her silver-white robe moving softly in the air. She raised one hand, and the randomizer slowed down slightly.
"The first main round will now begin," she said clearly. "There will be fifty battles in this round. Fifty participants will advance, and fifty participants will be eliminated."
The moment her voice fell, the atmosphere around the one hundred pillars changed.
Even the relaxed participants became serious.

This was no longer the chaotic first round where people could retreat, hide, ambush, or wait for better chances. Here, a name would be called, a person would appear on the stage, and the result would decide whether that person continued in the Cosmic Ascension Conference or left completely.
The randomizer stopped.
Two names shone brightly above the arena.
[Battle One]
[Calder Vayne vs Mirella Thorn]
Angelina glanced at the names and spoke calmly. "Calder Vayne. Mirella Thorn. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended from separate pillars and wrapped around two participants.

One was a tall young man wearing black armor, holding a heavy axe covered in flame markings. The other was a green-haired woman holding a thin spear, her body surrounded by faint wind currents. Both appeared on opposite sides of the central stage, and the transparent barrier around the arena brightened at once.
[Battle One Begins.]

Calder Vayne acted first. He stomped forward, and flames rose from his axe as he swung it down with brute force. Mirella Thorn did not meet him head-on. She moved like a shadow carried by the wind, avoiding the axe by a narrow margin before thrusting her spear toward his shoulder.
Calder roared, turned his body, and let the spear scrape against his armor before countering with another heavy swing.
The battle was fierce but not shocking compared to the monsters everyone had seen before.
After nearly a hundred exchanges, Mirella finally found a gap in Calder’s defense. Her spear pierced through the joint of his armor and stopped at his throat before he could lift his axe again.
Angelina’s voice rang out.
[Winner: Mirella Thorn.]
[Calder Vayne Eliminated.]

A beam of light swallowed Calder before he could say anything, removing him from the stage. Mirella returned to her pillar, breathing heavily but smiling with relief. The first battle had ended, and the number of participants who could advance had already begun to shrink.
The randomizer spun again.
[Battle Two]
[Varun Eclipsar vs Thalia Mooncrest]

A young man covered in dark blue starlight appeared on the stage opposite a woman with moon-white hair and silver daggers. Their battle was much faster than the first. Varun used long-range eclipse spells, trying to force Thalia to keep her distance, but Thalia’s movement technique was strange. She stepped in and out of moonlight, closing the gap again and again until her dagger touched the center of Varun’s chest.
[Winner: Thalia Mooncrest.]
[Varun Eclipsar Eliminated.]
The second battle ended cleanly.
The randomizer spun again.
[Battle Three]
[Gorath Ironhide vs Elian Vale]
This time, the fight drew more attention.

Gorath was a massive beastman with bronze skin and a body like a mountain, while Elian Vale was a slender young man dressed in scholar-like white robes. At first glance, many people assumed Gorath would crush him quickly, but once the battle began, Elian revealed terrifying control over runic chains. Each time Gorath tried to charge, golden chains rose from the stage and slowed his movements.

Gorath endured three rounds of binding and finally tore through the runes with raw strength, but Elian had already prepared his final technique. A formation circle opened beneath Gorath’s feet, and countless chains wrapped around his limbs, neck, and waist at the same time.
Gorath struggled violently, but he could not break free before Elian’s palm stopped in front of his forehead.
[Winner: Elian Vale.]
[Gorath Ironhide Eliminated.]
On the pillars, many participants began whispering.
"These battles are not weak."
"Of course they are not weak. Everyone here survived until the final hundred."
"But the randomizer is clearly avoiding the top monsters for now."

"That is normal. If Damian Voss, Orion Starfall, Rakan Thorne, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, or Max Morgan meet each other in the first elimination stage, the final ranking will become strange. The real monsters should collide later."
Max stood on his pillar and listened quietly.
He had also noticed the pattern.

The randomizer did not seem completely ordinary. It called itself random, but there was likely some hidden rule preventing the most famous top-tier geniuses from encountering each other too early. That made sense. The Cosmic Ascension Conference wanted a proper final ranking, not a situation where several peak monsters eliminated each other before the final twenty-five even formed.
Angelina Valerius showed no reaction to the whispers.
The randomizer spun again.
The sixth battle came next.
[Battle Six]
[Toren Ashguard vs Bellara Sain]

This was a battle between a shield user and a healer-type combatant who used light-based restraints. Many people expected it to last a long time, and it did. Toren’s defense was extremely strong, and Bellara could not break it easily, but Bellara was clever. Instead of trying to destroy his shield, she used her light restraints to bind his feet, then his arms, then slowly forced him into a position where he could no longer move properly.
In the end, Toren surrendered with a helpless expression.
[Winner: Bellara Sain.]
[Toren Ashguard Eliminated.]
Rakan Thorne yawned from his pillar. "These fights are not bad, but when are they going to call someone interesting?"
Orion Starfall smiled from a nearby pillar. "Be patient. The stage is warming up."

Damian Voss stood silently, eyes half-closed as if none of these battles interested him. Kaiden Voidmere watched calmly, while Ervin seemed to be studying every participant’s habits without showing much emotion. Princess Rosaline observed the flow of battles with a thoughtful expression, perhaps memorizing who might become troublesome in later rounds.

Rose stood on her own pillar in the distance. She had not been called yet, but her expression was serious. She knew she had survived the first round mostly through careful movement and good judgment. In a direct battle, luck would not help her as much.

chapters.title: Chapter 1820: First Round - 2
paragraphs: The randomizer spun again.
[Battle Seven]
[Hector Marrow vs Yulina Starbloom]

Hector was a bone-armored warrior with a cruel fighting style, while Yulina used star-thread techniques that looked delicate but were extremely dangerous. Hector tried to overwhelm her with brutal attacks, but Yulina’s star threads gradually wrapped around his weapon, then his arms, then his body. The more he struggled, the tighter the threads became.
After a short but intense fight, Yulina’s star threads forced Hector’s knees to bend, and a shining thread stopped at his neck.
[Winner: Yulina Starbloom.]
[Hector Marrow Eliminated.]
The eighth battle was even faster.
[Battle Eight]
[Draven Hollow vs Mirael Sunveil]

Draven attempted to use illusion techniques, but Mirael’s sunfire burned through his false images almost immediately. Within twenty exchanges, he was forced off balance and defeated by a palm of golden flame.
[Winner: Mirael Sunveil.]
[Draven Hollow Eliminated.]
As battle after battle passed, the tension in the arena continued to build.
The top geniuses had not moved yet.
Damian Voss remained on his pillar.
Rakan Thorne remained on his pillar.

Orion Starfall, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rosaline, and several other frightening figures were still waiting. Even Max had not been called. That made many people even more nervous because each spin of the randomizer could drag any one of them onto the stage.
Then the randomizer spun for the ninth time.
The golden names moved faster than before.
Finally, two names stopped and enlarged above the stage.
[Battle Nine]
[Max Morgan vs Arvian Dreadspire]
The entire arena fell silent for a breath.
Then the whispers erupted.
"Max Morgan."
"It is his turn already."
"Who is Arvian Dreadspire?"
"I have heard of him. He is from the Dreadspire Clan, a powerful demon-blooded family. He survived the first round by hunting smaller groups alone."
"That is unlucky for him."
"Do not say that too quickly. Anyone who reached the final hundred is not weak."
On his pillar, Max looked at the name calmly.

Arvian Dreadspire stood on another pillar across the arena. He was a tall young man with ash-gray skin, black horns, and dark red markings crawling across his neck. His aura was gloomy and heavy, and when he saw that his opponent was Max, his expression became extremely ugly for a moment before he forced himself to calm down.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both of them.
"Max Morgan. Arvian Dreadspire. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
Max did not resist the transfer.

The next moment, he appeared on one side of the central arena, Dragonheart resting quietly at his waist. Opposite him, Arvian appeared with a long black spear in his hand. The barrier around the central stage lit up again, and the names above the arena glowed brightly.
[Battle Nine Begins.]
Arvian stared at Max with a solemn expression.

He knew Max’s reputation. Everyone here knew Max’s reputation by now. But surrendering without fighting was not something he could accept. He had survived the first round, reached the final hundred, and carried the pride of his clan. Even if he lost, he had to at least make a move.
Max looked at him calmly.
"Are you going to surrender?" he asked.
Arvian’s face twitched slightly.
"Do not look down on me too much, Max Morgan."
Max smiled faintly. "Then come."
On the pillars, everyone focused their attention on the stage.
Arvian Dreadspire tightened his grip around his long black spear.

He had already heard too many rumors about Max Morgan, and none of them were comforting. Some said Max had killed Selene Vaeloria. Some said he had forced Seraphine and Fin to end themselves. Some said he had cut down Morgana Starveil from Stellar Templar with one sword.

Some said he had exchanged sword moves with Damian Voss without losing. Arvian did not know which rumors were exaggerated and which were true, but standing opposite Max on the central stage, he understood one thing clearly. The white-haired young man before him did not look nervous at all.
That calmness made Arvian even more uneasy.
"Do not think I will go down easily," Arvian said in a deep voice.
Max looked at him calmly. "Then show me."
Arvian roared.

Dark red energy erupted from his body, and the markings on his neck spread across his face like burning cracks. He stomped forward, and the entire central stage trembled under his charge. His spear stabbed out like a black dragon, carrying a heavy demonic pressure that would have forced most opponents to retreat instantly.
Max did not move.
The spear arrived before him in an instant.
Only then did Max raise his hand.
He did not draw Dragonheart.
He simply stretched out two fingers and caught the spearhead between them.
The arena fell silent.

Arvian’s expression changed wildly. He pushed forward with both hands, but the spear did not move at all. It was as if the weapon had been nailed into the void by Max’s fingers. The dark red energy around the spear surged violently, but Max’s hand remained steady, and his expression did not change in the slightest.
"What?" Arvian muttered in disbelief.
Max looked at him. "Too weak."
Before Arvian could react, Max twisted his fingers.
Crack!
The spearhead shattered.

Arvian’s eyes widened, but Max had already stepped forward. His movement was not flashy. It was not even particularly exaggerated. He simply crossed the distance between them in one step and struck Arvian’s chest with his palm.
Boom!
Arvian’s body flew backward like a broken meteor.

He crashed into the barrier at the edge of the arena, and the impact made the entire protective dome ripple violently. Blood sprayed from his mouth, and the dark red markings across his body dimmed at once. He tried to stand, but his knees buckled before he could stabilize himself.
Max remained where he was.
From beginning to end, he had not drawn Dragonheart.
The sight made many participants on the pillars fall completely silent.
Angelina Valerius glanced at Arvian for a moment, then announced calmly, "Arvian Dreadspire is unable to continue."
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Arvian Dreadspire Eliminated.]
A beam of light descended and removed Arvian from the stage.

Max was transferred back to his pillar a moment later, his expression calm as if the battle had not even warmed him up. The participants who had been wondering whether his reputation was exaggerated could no longer say anything.
Even if Arvian was not one of the peak monsters, he had still survived until the final hundred. Yet against Max, he had not even been able to force Dragonheart out of its sheath.

"That is unlucky for him."
"Do not say that too quickly.
Anyone who reached the final hundred is not weak."
On his pillar, Max looked at the name calmly.
Arvian Dreadspire stood on another pillar across the arena.
He was a tall young man with ash-gray skin, black horns, and dark red markings crawling across his neck.
His aura was gloomy and heavy, and when he saw that his opponent was Max, his expression became extremely ugly for a moment before he forced himself to calm down.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both of them.
"Max Morgan.
Arvian Dreadspire.
Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
Max did not resist the transfer.
The next moment, he appeared on one side of the central arena, Dragonheart resting quietly at his waist.
Opposite him, Arvian appeared with a long black spear in his hand.
The barrier around the central stage lit up again, and the names above the arena glowed brightly.
[Battle Nine Begins.]
Arvian stared at Max with a solemn expression.
He knew Max’s reputation.
Everyone here knew Max’s reputation by now.
But surrendering without fighting was not something he could accept.
He had survived the first round, reached the final hundred, and carried the pride of his clan.
Even if he lost, he had to at least make a move.
Max looked at him calmly.
"Are you going to surrender?" he asked.
Arvian’s face twitched slightly.
"Do not look down on me too much, Max Morgan."
Max smiled faintly.
"Then come."
On the pillars, everyone focused their attention on the stage.
Arvian Dreadspire tightened his grip around his long black spear.
He had already heard too many rumors about Max Morgan, and none of them were comforting.
Some said Max had killed Selene Vaeloria.
Some said he had forced Seraphine and Fin to end themselves.
Some said he had cut down Morgana Starveil from Stellar Templar with one sword.
Some said he had exchanged sword moves with Damian Voss without losing.
Arvian did not know which rumors were exaggerated and which were true, but standing opposite Max on the central stage, he understood one thing clearly.
The white-haired young man before him did not look nervous at all.
That calmness made Arvian even more uneasy.
"Do not think I will go down easily," Arvian said in a deep voice.
Max looked at him calmly.
"Then show me."
Arvian roared.
Dark red energy erupted from his body, and the markings on his neck spread across his face like burning cracks.
He stomped forward, and the entire central stage trembled under his charge.
His spear stabbed out like a black dragon, carrying a heavy demonic pressure that would have forced most opponents to retreat instantly.
Max did not move.
The spear arrived before him in an instant.
Only then did Max raise his hand.
He did not draw Dragonheart.
He simply stretched out two fingers and caught the spearhead between them.
The arena fell silent.
Arvian’s expression changed wildly.
He pushed forward with both hands, but the spear did not move at all.
It was as if the weapon had been nailed into the void by Max’s fingers.
The dark red energy around the spear surged violently, but Max’s hand remained steady, and his expression did not change in the slightest.
"What?" Arvian muttered in disbelief.
Max looked at him.
"Too weak."
Before Arvian could react, Max twisted his fingers.
Crack!
The spearhead shattered.
Arvian’s eyes widened, but Max had already stepped forward.
His movement was not flashy.
It was not even particularly exaggerated.
He simply crossed the distance between them in one step and struck Arvian’s chest with his palm.
Boom!
Arvian’s body flew backward like a broken meteor.
He crashed into the barrier at the edge of the arena, and the impact made the entire protective dome ripple violently.
Blood sprayed from his mouth, and the dark red markings across his body dimmed at once.
He tried to stand, but his knees buckled before he could stabilize himself.
Max remained where he was.
From beginning to end, he had not drawn Dragonheart.
The sight made many participants on the pillars fall completely silent.
Angelina Valerius glanced at Arvian for a moment, then announced calmly, "Arvian Dreadspire is unable to continue."
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Arvian Dreadspire Eliminated.]
A beam of light descended and removed Arvian from the stage.
Max was transferred back to his pillar a moment later, his expression calm as if the battle had not even warmed him up.
The participants who had been wondering whether his reputation was exaggerated could no longer say anything.
Even if Arvian was not one of the peak monsters, he had still survived until the final hundred.
Yet against Max, he had not even been able to force Dragonheart out of its sheath.

chapters.title: Chapter 1821: First Round - 3
paragraphs: Rakan Thorne laughed from his pillar. "That was too fast. At least let the man show one more move."
Orion Starfall smiled faintly. "He did show one move. It was just not enough."
Princess Rosaline’s eyes remained on Max. "His physical strength is also terrifying. He defeated a demon-blooded spear user without using his sword, bloodline, or any visible path."
Kaiden Voidmere watched Max quietly and said nothing, but his gaze became deeper.
Ervin smiled faintly. "He is hiding far more than the others realize."

Damian Voss opened his eyes from his pillar and looked at Max for a moment. His expression did not change much, but the sharpness in his gaze increased. He had already acknowledged Max’s swordsmanship earlier, but now he had seen that Max’s combat foundation was not limited to the sword. That made him even more difficult to measure.
Angelina raised her hand again.
The randomizer spun.
Several more battles passed after Max’s victory.

Some were fierce, some were brief, and some ended with surrender the moment the weaker participant realized the gap. The arena continued eliminating names one after another, and the number of qualified participants slowly moved toward fifty.
Then the randomizer stopped again.
[Battle Fourteen]
[Damian Voss vs Soren Blackwater]
The entire arena became alert at once.
Damian Voss finally stood from his pillar.

His opponent, Soren Blackwater, was a black-robed man with water-like shadows surrounding his body. He had survived the first round through assassination techniques and strange movement, and his aura was slippery and difficult to lock onto. However, the moment he saw that his opponent was Damian, his face became extremely solemn.
Two beams of light descended.
Damian appeared on the stage with his sword resting at his side.

Soren appeared opposite him and immediately spread his shadow-water aura across the ground. A dark mist covered his body, and in the next instant, he split into several afterimages, each one rushing toward Damian from a different direction.
Damian did not move.
His sword left its sheath by an inch.
A clean sword light flashed.
All the afterimages were cut apart at the same time.
Soren’s real body appeared behind Damian with a dagger aimed at his back, but before the dagger could land, Damian’s sword was already touching Soren’s throat.
No one saw when he had turned.
No one saw when the blade had fully left its sheath.
Soren froze.
Damian said calmly, "You lose."
Angelina’s voice followed immediately.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Soren Blackwater Eliminated.]
The crowd on the pillars became silent again.

Max watched calmly from his pillar. Damian had not used any Pseudo Cosmic Path. He had not even shown his real sword concept. Just one clean sword movement had ended the battle. His sword was simple, direct, and terrifyingly precise.
Compared to the flashy sword light many swordsmen preferred, Damian’s sword felt far more dangerous because every movement existed only to end the fight.
’His sword is extremely refined,’ Max thought while watching Damian return to his pillar. ’He does not waste a single movement.’
The randomizer continued.
[Battle Seventeen]
[Rakan Thorne vs Yelric Flamehorn]

Rakan’s opponent was a horned fire-attribute warrior with a massive flaming halberd. Yelric Flamehorn clearly knew he could not hold back against someone like Rakan, so the moment the battle began, he released all his flame power and charged forward with a roar.
Rakan grinned and walked toward him barehanded.
The flaming halberd descended.
Rakan punched it.
The weapon bent.

Yelric’s face changed, but Rakan’s second punch had already landed on his stomach. The fire around Yelric’s body exploded outward, then scattered completely as his body folded around Rakan’s fist. He flew backward, crashed into the arena floor, and rolled several dozen times before stopping.
Rakan shook his hand as if disappointed.
"That is it?"
Angelina’s voice rang out.
[Winner: Rakan Thorne.]
[Yelric Flamehorn Eliminated.]
Max observed Rakan quietly.

Rakan’s strength was straightforward but horrifying. He did not rely on tricks, but his raw body, war aura, and combat instincts were so overwhelming that ordinary geniuses could not even force him to defend. If Damian’s sword was refined to the extreme, then Rakan’s fists were the opposite. They were blunt, brutal, and absolute.
The next top genius to be called was Princess Rosaline.
[Battle Twenty-One]
[Rosaline Lunara vs Cressa Thornveil]

Rosaline appeared on the central stage with graceful calm, her white and rose-gold gown moving softly around her. Cressa Thornveil was a poison vine user who immediately tried to fill the arena with thorny roots and dark green mist. However, Rosaline only lifted one hand, and gentle golden-pink light spread outward like dawn touching the earth.
The poison mist dissolved.
The thorny vines withered.
Cressa tried to summon more, but Rosaline’s light had already formed a radiant cage around her.
The battle ended without Rosaline taking a single step.
[Winner: Rosaline Lunara.]
[Cressa Thornveil Eliminated.]
Several participants looked uneasy.

Max watched with interest. Rosaline’s power did not feel aggressive at first, but its suppression was extremely clean. It purified, restrained, and sealed at the same time. Against many opponents, she would not need to overpower them directly. She only needed to remove the foundation of their techniques and trap them afterward.
’Not bad,’ Max thought.
Soon after, Orion Starfall’s name appeared.
[Battle Twenty-Five]
[Orion Starfall vs Marek Ironstorm]

Orion entered the stage with the same warm smile on his face. His opponent, Marek Ironstorm, wielded a pair of heavy gauntlets and controlled storm-metal energy. Marek clearly did not want to lose without trying, so he attacked with full force as soon as Angelina announced the start.
Thunder roared.
Metallic storm clouds gathered above the stage.
Orion looked up and smiled. "Nice weather."
Then one of the nine star marks on his body lit up.
A single star beam descended.

It pierced through the storm clouds, shattered Marek’s gauntlet aura, and stopped just in front of his forehead. The beam did not touch him, but the pressure alone forced Marek’s entire body to stiffen.
Marek stared at the light in front of his face and slowly raised his hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina nodded.
[Winner: Orion Starfall.]
[Marek Ironstorm Eliminated.]
Rakan laughed from his pillar. "You are still pretending to be harmless."
Orion returned to his pillar and smiled. "I am harmless when people surrender quickly."

chapters.title: Chapter 1822: First Round - 4
paragraphs: Max looked at him for a few breaths.

Orion had used only one star mark, and even that had not revealed much. But the precision, speed, and pressure of that single beam were enough to show why he was considered one of the strongest geniuses of the Nine Star Court. His strength was not only destructive. It was controlled.
Then came Kaiden Voidmere.
[Battle Twenty-Nine]
[Kaiden Voidmere vs Liora Sunshard]

Kaiden’s opponent was a woman with radiant sunfire wings. She did not underestimate him. The moment the battle began, she rose into the air and released dozens of golden fire feathers, each one carrying enough heat to burn through divine metal.
Kaiden stood still.
The fire feathers reached him.
Then they vanished.
There was no explosion. No impact. No clash.
They simply disappeared into faint ripples of void.

Liora’s expression changed, and she immediately tried to retreat, but the space behind her quietly folded. Kaiden appeared there as if he had never moved, one finger already touching the back of her neck.
"You lose," he said calmly.
Liora’s face turned pale.
[Winner: Kaiden Voidmere.]
[Liora Sunshard Eliminated.]
Max narrowed his eyes slightly.

Kaiden’s use of void power was extremely clean. It was different from ordinary space manipulation. It felt deeper, quieter, and more absolute. Since Kaiden had already sensed the Void Genesis Art in him and called him junior brother in a roundabout way, Max had been paying closer attention to him.
Now, after seeing this battle, Max was even more certain that Kaiden was not simple.
’His void path is far ahead of mine,’ Max thought.
Not long after, Ervin’s name appeared.
[Battle Thirty-Two]
[Ervin vs Darius Stoneveil]

Darius Stoneveil was a defensive cultivator with an earthstone body. The moment he entered the stage, stone armor covered him from head to toe, and layers of heavy barriers rose around him. It was clear that he wanted to survive long enough to find an opening.
Ervin walked forward with his black spear in hand.
There was no violent aura at first.
Only a faint darkness gathered around the spear tip.
Darius roared and strengthened his barriers.
Ervin thrust once.

The black spear pierced through the first barrier, then the second, then the third, then the stone armor, stopping just before Darius’s chest. Every layer had been penetrated in a straight line, as if the spear had ignored the distance between them and gone directly to its target.
Darius froze.
Ervin withdrew his spear calmly.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Darius Stoneveil Eliminated.]
Max’s expression became a little more focused.

He had fought Ervin in the Genesis Trial, so he already knew Ervin was dangerous. But outside the trial, Ervin’s abyssal spear still carried that same strange depth. It did not look overwhelming, but once it moved, it seemed to sink through all defenses until it reached the core.
’Still hiding most of his strength,’ Max thought.
Battle after battle continued.
More names were called. More participants were eliminated. Some battles lasted long enough to draw attention, while others ended in a few moves when the difference in strength was too large.

As the first main round progressed, it became clear that the strongest geniuses were being preserved for later clashes. Damian, Rakan, Rosaline, Orion, Kaiden, Ervin, and Max had all won without revealing their true trump cards.
On the pillars, the participants who had advanced watched the remaining battles with heavier expressions.
The weaker half of the final hundred was being removed.
The arena was becoming more dangerous with every victory.
Max stood quietly on his pillar, observing everything.

He had seen Damian’s refined sword, Rakan’s brutal fists, Rosaline’s radiant suppression, Orion’s star power, Kaiden’s void control, and Ervin’s abyssal spear. None of them had revealed their Pseudo Cosmic Paths or deepest foundations yet, but even the small glimpse they had shown was enough to prove one thing.
The final round would not be boring.
Max’s gaze swept across the pillars of the top geniuses, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
The first elimination stage was only the beginning.
The real battles were still waiting ahead.
The randomizer continued spinning after Ervin’s battle.

Several more names flashed across the light screen before finally slowing down again. This time, when the two names appeared, many participants instinctively turned their attention toward one particular pillar.
[Battle Thirty-Five]
[Revona vs Caelum Brightforge]
The moment Revona’s name appeared, Max’s eyes shifted toward her.

Revona stood silently on her pillar, her long hair moving slightly in the faint wind of the arena. Her expression was calm, almost indifferent, and her eyes were still closed. She had not shown much presence since the final round began, but Max had never underestimated her. He had fought her before, and he knew better than most people here how strange and dangerous her Void Origin Eyes could be.

Caelum Brightforge, on the other hand, was a tall young man wearing golden armor. A blazing hammer rested on his shoulder, and his aura carried the heat and weight of divine flame mixed with forging power.

From the whispers around the pillars, Max quickly learned that Caelum was a famous genius from an ancient blacksmith clan, someone who combined weapon refinement, fire control, and body tempering into one combat style.
Angelina Valerius looked at both of them calmly.
"Revona. Caelum Brightforge. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Revona appeared on one side of the central arena, her eyes still closed, while Caelum appeared opposite her with his golden hammer in hand. The barrier around the arena brightened again, and the runes across the stage lit up beneath their feet.
Caelum looked at Revona seriously.
"I have heard of your eyes," he said. "I know they are dangerous."
Revona’s voice was calm. "Then you should attack with everything from the beginning."
Caelum’s expression became sharper. "That was my plan."
[Battle Thirty-Five Begins.]
Caelum moved first.

Flames erupted from his golden armor, and the hammer in his hand expanded in size as if it had awakened from a dormant state. He stomped on the ground and rushed forward, each step leaving behind a burning footprint on the arena floor. The temperature inside the barrier rose sharply, and a wave of golden fire surged behind him like a furnace being opened.
"Divine Forge Hammer, First Strike!"
His hammer descended with terrifying force.

The attack was powerful enough to make many participants narrow their eyes. It carried both brute strength and flame pressure, and as the hammer fell, the air itself seemed to be compressed into a burning wave.

Then the whispers exploded.
"What just happened?"
"His attack disappeared?"
"No, it did not disappear normally. It was nullified."
"That is the Void Origin Eyes?"

Caelum’s expression changed greatly, but he reacted quickly. He pulled back his hammer and spun in place, releasing a ring of golden fire around his body. Several flame-forged weapons appeared in the air, including spears, swords, axes, and chains, all burning with the same divine forging flame.
"Let me see how many attacks you can erase at once!"
He roared and swung his hammer forward.
The flame-forged weapons shot toward Revona from every direction.
Revona stood still.
Her Void Origin Eyes glowed deeper.
One spear vanished.
Then one sword.
Then three axes disappeared at the same time.

A chain reached her ankle, but the moment it entered the range of her gaze, the burning links broke apart into faint void ripples. The remaining weapons circled around her, trying to attack from angles outside her direct line of sight, but Revona only turned her head slightly. Wherever her eyes passed, the attacks were erased.
Max’s gaze sharpened.
This was different.
When he had fought Revona before, her Void Origin Eyes had already been powerful, but they had not been this smooth.

Back then, there had been limits. Her eyes could make attacks turn into nothingness, but the timing, range, and control had not reached this level. If someone attacked fast enough, with enough physical power, or from a close enough distance, she could still be forced into a difficult situation.
But now, her eyes had clearly awakened further.
Caelum also realized this.

His expression became ugly as he backed away and raised his hammer with both hands. The golden armor on his body opened slightly, releasing streams of blazing light, and a massive furnace image appeared behind him. The furnace roared with fire, and countless divine runes appeared across the hammer’s surface.
The participants on the pillars became serious.
"He is using his strongest technique."
"That furnace image is not ordinary. It should be the core inheritance of the Brightforge Clan."
"If even this gets erased, then her eyes are too unreasonable."
Caelum roared, "Divine Forge Hammer, Heaven-Melting Descent!"
The massive furnace image poured all its flames into the hammer.
Then Caelum leapt into the air and smashed downward.

This strike was far stronger than all his previous attacks combined. The hammer carried enough heat to distort the stage itself, and the golden flames condensed into a giant burning hammer that descended like a falling sun. Even through the barrier, many participants felt a wave of heat brush against them.
Revona looked up.
Her eyes remained calm.
The void-colored light in her pupils expanded.
The falling sun touched her gaze.
Then a hole appeared in it.

The golden hammer image lost its center first. Then the surrounding flames collapsed inward. The heat vanished. The pressure vanished. The divine runes vanished. The entire technique, which had been powerful enough to threaten most participants in the final hundred, disappeared before it could touch her.
Caelum fell from the air, his face pale.

His real hammer was still in his hand, but the strongest force behind the strike had been nullified completely. Before he could stabilize himself, Revona appeared in front of him with one finger raised toward his forehead.
She had not even used a weapon.
Caelum froze.
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Revona.]
[Caelum Brightforge Eliminated.]
A beam of light descended and removed Caelum from the stage.
Revona closed her eyes again and returned to her pillar.
For a few seconds, no one spoke.
Then the arena erupted into discussion.
"That is ridiculous."
"How are you supposed to fight her if your attacks disappear before reaching her?"
"Caelum Brightforge was not weak at all. His strongest strike was erased like smoke."
"She did not even look tired."
"Those eyes are terrifying."
Max stood on his pillar and watched Revona silently.

His expression did not show fear, but his eyes had become more serious. He remembered his earlier battle with her very clearly. At that time, he had defeated her because of his overwhelming physical strength and because her Void Origin Eyes had not fully awakened. He had closed the distance, pressured her body, and forced her into a situation where her eyes could not completely erase his raw power before he overwhelmed her.
But now things would not be so simple.
Her eyes had grown stronger.

Their range had improved. Their stability had improved. Their ability to nullify attacks from multiple directions had improved. Most importantly, she seemed much calmer while using them, which meant the burden on her body might have decreased as well.
’If I fight her again, relying only on brute force will not be enough,’ Max thought.
He looked at Revona’s closed eyes.
’Last time, I defeated her before those eyes could truly control the battle. Now, if she opens them properly, every attack I use might be erased before it reaches her.’
For a moment, Max imagined how his different powers would fare against her.
Ordinary sword light would likely be nullified.
Divine King Punishment might be erased if it entered her gaze directly.
Even space-based movements could become risky if her eyes could target the origin of the movement rather than the movement itself.
As for Emotion Severing Path, Max was not sure.
That uncertainty made his interest grow.
On another pillar, Damian Voss also looked toward Revona with a rare serious expression.
"Void Origin Eyes," he murmured. "So they have awakened to that level."
Orion Starfall’s smile became thoughtful. "This conference really has too many troublesome people."
Rakan Thorne grinned, but even he looked more focused than before. "So if I punch her, will the punch disappear, or will her eyes fail before my fist reaches her?"
Ervin glanced at him and said calmly, "That depends on whether your fist reaches her before she sees enough of it."
Rakan laughed. "Then I just need to punch faster."

Kaiden Voidmere watched Revona quietly, his silver-gray eyes reflecting a faint void light of their own. Unlike the others, his reaction was harder to read, but Max could tell that he was paying attention. As someone connected to the void path himself, Kaiden likely understood more about Revona’s eyes than most people here.
Princess Rosaline’s expression also became solemn.
"Her eyes are almost unfair in direct combat," one of the Lunarian geniuses beside her said.
Rosaline nodded slightly. "Almost. But no power is truly without weakness. The problem is whether anyone here can find it before losing."
Revona returned to her pillar and remained silent, as if the battle had not mattered much to her.
Max watched her for a moment longer before looking back at the central stage.
The final round was becoming more interesting.
Damian’s sword was terrifying.
Rakan’s body was overwhelming.
Orion’s star power was precise and controlled.
Kaiden’s void was deep and quiet.
Ervin’s abyssal spear was strange and dangerous.
Rosaline’s radiant suppression was extremely clean.
And Revona’s Void Origin Eyes could nullify attacks as if they had never existed.
Max smiled faintly.
The first main round had not even ended yet, but the true threats were already revealing themselves one by one.
And that made the coming battles worth waiting for.

chapters.title: Chapter 1824: First Round - 6
paragraphs: After Revona returned to her pillar, the atmosphere around the arena remained strange for quite some time.

Her battle had not been long, but its impact was far greater than many of the longer battles before it. Caelum Brightforge had not been weak. His forging flame, hammer technique, and defensive foundation were all strong enough to place him above most ordinary geniuses, yet every attack he used had simply disappeared before Revona’s Void Origin Eyes.
That kind of power made many participants feel uncomfortable because it was difficult to understand and even harder to counter.
Max watched her for a while before shifting his gaze back to the central stage.
The randomizer continued spinning.

Battle after battle unfolded before him, and Max observed each one with calm attention. Most fights were between geniuses he did not recognize, but none of them were truly weak. A silver-armored knight defeated a beast-blooded archer by closing the distance in three breaths.

A shadow cultivator lost to a woman who controlled sound waves because his stealth became useless the moment her spiritual perception spread through vibration. A flame user fought a water user for nearly half an hour before finally winning by exhausting his opponent’s reserves. Each battle showed a different path, different foundation, and different weakness.
Max did not watch casually.

His Dimensional Sovereign Body allowed him to perceive details others missed. He noticed how some people hid injuries behind stable breathing, how some used feints to draw out trump cards, how some carried strength far above what their surface aura suggested, and how some were already thinking about later rounds even while fighting their current opponent. This final round was not merely a place to win battles. It was also a place to study future enemies.
Then the randomizer stopped again.
[Battle Thirty-Eight]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Kovan Ashrune]
The name made Max’s eyes turn cold.
Aurelian Lareth.
The Divine Son of the second elven faction.
The one who had received Max’s stolen Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.

The moment that name appeared, many participants turned toward one of the pillars. A young man stood there in white-gold robes, his long golden hair falling behind him, his face handsome and almost too perfect. His eyes carried a sacred radiance, and a faint divine light flowed around his body even though he had not released any power.

Compared to Selene’s pure and noble aura, Aurelian’s presence felt deeper, heavier, and more complete, as if something precious and powerful had been forcefully rooted inside him and cultivated for years.
Max stared at him silently.
Aurelian seemed to sense his gaze and turned his head.
Their eyes met across the arena.
For a brief moment, the air between their pillars seemed to freeze.
Aurelian smiled faintly.

It was not a friendly smile. It was calm, distant, and filled with an arrogance that came from knowing exactly what he possessed. His gaze briefly moved across Max’s body, as if he was studying the true owner of the bloodline inside him, and then he turned away as though Max could wait.
Max’s fingers moved slightly.
Angelina Valerius spoke calmly. "Aurelian Lareth. Kovan Ashrune. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Aurelian appeared on the central stage with both hands behind his back. Kovan Ashrune, his opponent, was a gray-robed man wielding a staff covered in ash-colored runes. The moment he saw Aurelian standing opposite him, his expression became extremely heavy. He knew very well that he had drawn one of the worst possible opponents.
[Battle Thirty-Eight Begins.]
Kovan acted immediately.

Ash-gray runes spread under his feet, and a storm of burning ash rose around him. The ash condensed into chains, spears, and shields, forming a battlefield that tried to suppress Aurelian from every direction. The technique was not weak. It carried both fire and decay, and if an ordinary opponent was trapped inside, their energy would be slowly burned away.
Aurelian did not move.
The moment the ash storm approached him, golden-white divine light spread from his body.
The ash chains dissolved.
The ash spears melted.
The entire burning field was purified in a single breath.

Kovan’s face changed, and he quickly raised his staff to form another rune array, but Aurelian simply lifted one finger. A beam of Heavenly Luminance light shot forward and pierced through the center of the rune array, shattering it before stopping an inch from Kovan’s forehead.
Kovan froze.
Aurelian’s voice was calm. "Surrender."
Kovan’s face turned pale. After a long breath, he lowered his staff.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Kovan Ashrune Eliminated.]
Aurelian returned to his pillar without even looking at his defeated opponent again.
Max’s eyes remained fixed on him.

The bloodline aura Aurelian had displayed was unmistakable. It was not exactly the same as Max’s current Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, but it was deeply connected to it. The second faction had stolen something from his body, and now they had raised Aurelian as the vessel for it. Seeing that divine light being used so calmly by someone else made Max’s gaze colder than before.
’So that is the Divine Son,’ Max thought. ’Good. I was wondering when I would meet him.’
Not long after Aurelian’s battle, another familiar name appeared.
[Battle Forty]
[Selene Vaeloria vs Dorian Frostmarch]
The atmosphere changed again.
The Divine Daughter of the second faction stepped onto the stage.

Selene Vaeloria looked almost unchanged from when Max had defeated her near the Witch God Tree. Her white-gold hair shone faintly, her eyes carried cold pride, and her aura was once again stable. The life-restoration rules of the Cosmic Ascension Conference had clearly allowed her to continue, and despite her previous defeat, she had still survived to enter the final hundred.
The moment she appeared, her gaze turned toward Max.
There was hatred in her eyes.
Not fear.
Hatred.
Max looked back at her calmly.
Selene did not speak, but her expression said enough. She had not forgotten the humiliation of being defeated by Max, nor the fact that he had shattered her superiority in front of so many people.

Her opponent, Dorian Frostmarch, was an ice-attribute swordsman. He released frost sword intent the moment the battle began, sending dozens of ice blades across the stage. The air turned cold, and crystalline snow spread across the arena floor.
Selene raised her hand.
Heavenly Luminance light unfolded behind her like a pair of radiant wings.
The frost sword intent was suppressed.

Dorian tried to force through with a stronger technique, forming a giant ice sword above his head, but Selene’s expression did not change. A golden-white wheel appeared behind her, spinning slowly with majestic pressure.
"Luminance Judgment."
The radiant wheel released a pillar of light.
Dorian’s ice sword shattered instantly.
The light stopped in front of his chest, burning through his defensive aura without touching his flesh. Dorian stared at the light, then slowly lowered his sword.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Selene Vaeloria.]
[Dorian Frostmarch Eliminated.]
Selene returned to her pillar, but before the transfer light faded completely, she looked at Max again.
Max only smiled faintly.
That smile made Selene’s expression turn even colder.

chapters.title: Chapter 1825: First Round - 7
paragraphs: The randomizer continued.
A few more battles passed.

Some participants were eliminated quickly, while others managed to advance after hard-fought clashes. A spearwoman with thunder wings defeated a poison cultivator by overwhelming him before his toxins could spread.

A demon youth with black flames lost to a calm monk-like participant who reflected his flame back through a strange palm art. A silver-haired beastkin girl surrendered after realizing that her opponent’s soul attacks had already trapped her in an illusion field.
Then another familiar name appeared.
[Battle Forty-Three]
[Morgana Starveil vs Elara Mistwood]
Max’s eyes shifted.

Morgana Starveil appeared on the stage with her midnight-blue hair, black-violet dress, and purple eyes. Her witch hat tilted slightly over her head, and her lips carried a faint smile, but that smile did not reach her eyes. She looked toward Max almost immediately after appearing.
Their gazes met.
Morgana’s smile widened.

Unlike Selene, there was no open hatred in her expression. Instead, there was resentment hidden beneath playful calm, along with a dangerous curiosity. Max had killed her before with one Emotion Severing Path slash, splitting her apart despite all her curse defenses. Yet here she was again, revived by the rules of the conference and standing among the final hundred.

Elara Mistwood, her opponent, was a graceful woman with green hair and forest-like energy around her body. She used wood spirit techniques, summoning vines, petals, and misty roots to surround Morgana from all sides.
Morgana laughed softly.
"Wood against a witch? How nostalgic."
Elara frowned and attacked first.

The vines moved like serpents, each one carrying spiritual poison. Mist spread across the stage, hiding dozens of thorned branches that shot toward Morgana’s body from blind spots. But Morgana merely raised one finger, and black-violet symbols appeared in the air around her.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Curse of the Wandering Root."
The vines stopped.
Then they turned around.

Elara’s expression changed as her own wood techniques twisted under Morgana’s curse and attacked her instead. She quickly tried to regain control, but Morgana’s second curse had already descended. Seven purple-black stars appeared above the stage, each one releasing thin curse threads that wrapped around Elara’s limbs and spirit energy.
Elara struggled, but the more she resisted, the tighter the curse became.
Morgana walked forward slowly and stopped in front of her.
"You should surrender before the curse reaches your soul."
Elara’s face turned pale. After a few breaths, she lowered her head.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Morgana Starveil.]
[Elara Mistwood Eliminated.]
Morgana returned to her pillar and looked at Max again.
This time, she placed one finger near her lips and smiled, as if telling him that their unfinished business would continue later.
Max’s expression remained calm.

Morgana was still dangerous. Her direct combat strength might not be as overwhelming as Damian or Rakan, but her curse methods were troublesome and unpredictable. If she was allowed time to prepare, she could turn a simple battle into a trap. Max had killed her once because he had given her three moves and then crushed her with Emotion Severing Path, but that did not mean she was weak. It only meant his path had been a terrible match for her.
The battles continued.
Max also saw Seraphine Lareth and Fin Arclight among the remaining hundred.

Seraphine fought a halberd user who relied on violent close combat. She did not look as arrogant as before, but her Radiant Judgment Path was still fierce. Golden judgment light descended again and again, forcing her opponent to retreat until he finally failed to block a radiant spear and was judged unable to continue.
[Winner: Seraphine Lareth.]

Fin’s battle came shortly after. His Pale Eclipse Path spread across the arena like a gray-white moon shadow, dulling his opponent’s senses and weakening the rhythm of their attacks. He did not win as explosively as Seraphine, but he won cleanly, trapping his opponent in an eclipse field before ending the battle with a blade of pale light.
[Winner: Fin Arclight.]
Max looked at both of them without much emotion.

He had already killed them before. He had even forced them to end themselves once. But because of the rules of the first round, they had survived and returned to the final hundred. That did not bother him. If anything, it made things simpler. The more second faction people remained in the final round, the more chances he had to crush them on a stage everyone could see.
Rose’s battle also appeared later.
[Battle Forty-Six]
[Rose Valen vs Iskar Duskfang]

Rose’s opponent was a wolf-blooded fighter with sharp claws and terrifying speed. From the beginning, it was clear that Rose was not stronger than him in raw power. Iskar moved faster, attacked harder, and forced her to defend almost immediately. Several people assumed Rose would lose quickly, but Max watched with interest.
Rose did not panic.

She used small movements, defensive talismans, and precise footwork to keep herself alive. She never tried to overpower Iskar. Instead, she slowly guided him toward certain positions on the stage. After dozens of exchanges, Iskar finally stepped into a hidden formation mark she had placed through earlier movements.
Light chains erupted from beneath him.
Iskar roared and tore through two of them, but that small delay was enough.
Rose appeared behind him and placed a short blade against his neck.
Angelina declared the result.
[Winner: Rose Valen.]
[Iskar Duskfang Eliminated.]
Max smiled faintly.

Rose had not survived this far by luck alone. Her strength was not the most overwhelming, but her judgment, patience, and preparation were excellent. She knew how to make stronger opponents fall into her rhythm, and in a tournament setting, that could be just as valuable as raw power.
More battles followed.
Max saw battles battles of Tamara, and other few geniuses he could recognize but for some reason he didn’t find the prince from the first faction who had warned him about Caroline.
’With his strength he should have survive to top 100.’ Max thought deeply. ’But why isn’t he here?’
Finally, after the fiftieth battle ended, the massive screen of light above the arena changed.
[First Main Round Completed.]
[Total Participants: 100]
[Eliminated Participants: 50]
[Remaining Participants: 50]
The arena became silent.
Half of the final hundred had been removed.

The pillars belonging to eliminated participants dimmed and sank into the darkness below, while the remaining fifty pillars glowed brighter. The circle around the central stage became wider and emptier, making the remaining figures stand out even more clearly.
Angelina Valerius looked over the survivors calmly.
"Congratulations. The first main round of the final round has concluded. The remaining fifty participants will advance to the second main round."
Max looked around at the remaining pillars. There were many he recognized among them.
Along with them, many hidden experts whose names Max had only learned through watching their battles had also advanced. The arena had become smaller in number but far more dangerous in quality.
Max’s gaze moved from one familiar enemy to another.
A faint smile appeared on his face.
The people he had defeated once were still here.
The people he had not yet fought were waiting too.
And from the second main round onward, the chance of avoiding dangerous opponents would become smaller and smaller.
Angelina raised her hand again, and the randomizer above the arena began to awaken for the next stage.
"The second main round will begin shortly," she announced. "Fifty participants will fight. Twenty-five will remain."
The pillars hummed.
The remaining participants became silent.
Max watched the randomizer begin to spin again.
The true pressure of the final round was finally beginning to descend.

chapters.title: Chapter 1826: Second Round - 1
paragraphs: The second main round continued with growing pressure.
After several top geniuses had already secured their victories, the remaining participants became even more tense.

Every battle now carried the weight of elimination. Winning meant entering the final competitive stage with the remaining twenty-five, while losing meant leaving the Cosmic Ascension Conference before the true ranking battles even began.
The randomizer spun again.
[Second Main Round, Battle Twelve]
[Max Morgan vs Veyron Soulbinder]
The moment Max’s name appeared, many eyes turned toward his pillar.
Max opened his eyes calmly.

His opponent, Veyron Soulbinder, stood on a distant pillar wearing dark purple robes. His face was pale, his body was thin, and several small black bells floated around him without any visible strings. Unlike brute-force fighters or elemental geniuses, his aura was quiet and eerie. It did not press against the body. It pressed against the mind.
Several participants immediately became serious.
"Veyron Soulbinder. He is the soul-bell user who forced his previous opponent to surrender without even touching him."
"His soul attacks are extremely troublesome. Physical defense is useless against him."
"This might not be easy for Max Morgan. Even if Max’s body is monstrous, soul attacks are different."
Max heard the whispers but remained calm.
Angelina Valerius looked at both of them.
"Max Morgan. Veyron Soulbinder. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Max appeared on one side of the central arena, while Veyron appeared opposite him. The floating black bells around Veyron began to spin slowly, releasing a faint ringing sound that made some spectators on the pillars frown even though the arena barrier blocked most of the power.
Veyron looked at Max and smiled faintly.
"Max Morgan, I know you are strong. Your body is strong. Your sword is strong. Your bloodline is strong. But strength of the body does not always protect the soul."
Max looked at him calmly. "Are you done?"
Veyron’s smile stiffened slightly.
Then the battle began.
[Battle Begins.]
Veyron attacked immediately.
The black bells around him rang at the same time.
Ding.

The sound was soft, but the moment it rang out, an invisible soul wave rushed toward Max. It did not travel through the air like ordinary sound. It pierced directly toward the soul, trying to bypass the body, bloodline, sword, and physical defenses entirely.
Several participants watched closely.
Damian Voss narrowed his eyes slightly.
Rakan Thorne frowned. "Soul attacks. Annoying."
Orion Starfall smiled faintly but focused more than before. "Let us see how Max deals with this."
Veyron’s soul wave reached Max. Then nothing happened.
Max stood in place without moving. His expression did not change at all.
Veyron’s eyes narrowed.
He rang the bells again.

This time, the sound became layered. Several soul waves overlapped, forming a strange illusionary field around Max. Within that field, ordinary opponents would hear countless whispers from their own memories, regrets, fears, and weaknesses. Their minds would become unstable, their movements would slow, and their souls would gradually be bound by the ringing bells.
But Max only looked at him.
The soul waves entered his body and vanished as if they had fallen into a boundless domain.
Veyron’s expression changed for the first time.
"What?"
Max’s eyes remained calm.
He had the Dimension of Soul.

Against ordinary soul attacks, his soul was not an exposed weakness. It was a dimension. A vast inner space. The moment Veyron’s attacks tried to invade, they were swallowed by that dimension before they could affect him. It was not that Max was simply resisting the soul attacks. The attacks could not even properly touch the core of his soul.
Veyron gritted his teeth and raised both hands.
The black bells multiplied.
Three became nine.
Nine became thirty-six.
All thirty-six bells rang at once, and the sound turned sharp enough to make the barrier around the stage ripple faintly.
"Soul-Burial Bell Formation!"

A dark purple formation opened beneath Max’s feet. Countless soul chains rose from it, attempting to bind his soul directly. At the same time, ghostly faces appeared in the air, whispering curses meant to shake his consciousness and drag him into a soul illusion.
Max finally moved. He took one step forward.
The soul chains touched him.
Then they broke apart.
The ghostly faces screamed without sound before being pulled into an invisible depth around Max’s body. The Soul-Burial Bell Formation trembled violently, then collapsed from the center outward.
Veyron staggered backward, blood flowing from the corner of his mouth.
The backlash had struck him.
The arena became silent.
"How is that possible?"
"Veyron’s soul attack failed completely."
"Not failed. It was swallowed."
"What kind of soul defense does Max Morgan have?"
On her pillar, Revona opened her eyes slightly.
Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze deepened.
Ervin smiled faintly. "So his soul is also not ordinary."
Rosaline looked at Max with visible surprise. "He really has too many foundations."
Aurelian Lareth’s eyes narrowed, and Selene Vaeloria’s expression became colder.
Veyron stared at Max with disbelief. "What are you?"
Max walked toward him.

Veyron quickly rang all the bells again, but the result did not change. Soul needles, soul chains, soul illusions, soul curses, and soul-burial sound waves all entered the invisible depth around Max and disappeared. Nothing reached him. Nothing slowed him. Nothing shook his consciousness.
For Veyron, it was like attacking an ocean with drops of rain.
Max appeared in front of him.
Veyron’s face turned pale.
Max lifted one hand and stopped his fingers an inch from Veyron’s forehead.
"Your attacks are useless against me."
Veyron clenched his fists, but after a few breaths, he lowered his head.
"I surrender."
Angelina announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Veyron Soulbinder Eliminated.]
Max returned to his pillar.
The entire arena looked at him differently now.

Until this point, most people had known that Max was physically terrifying, possessed Dragonheart, had a dangerous sword path, and carried mysterious bloodline power. But now, they had seen that even soul attacks were almost useless against him. A participant who had specialized in attacking the soul had been completely restrained without Max even drawing his sword.

paragraphs: Max stood calmly on his pillar, as if the battle had not mattered much.
But many others were no longer calm.
Rakan Thorne clicked his tongue. "Body is monstrous. Sword is monstrous. Soul defense is monstrous. Does this guy have a normal weakness?"
Orion Starfall smiled. "If he does, he is hiding it well."
Damian Voss looked at Max in silence, his gaze sharper than before.
Kaiden Voidmere murmured softly, "Dimension of Soul?"
Ervin heard those words and glanced toward Kaiden, but Kaiden did not explain further.
Max ignored the reactions and looked back at the central stage.
The randomizer continued.
Aurelian Lareth was called soon after.
[Second Main Round, Battle Thirteen]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Corvin Nightsteel]

Corvin Nightsteel was not weak. He used dark metal armor and a heavy sword, and his first attack released a black storm of blade fragments that covered half the stage. Against most opponents, the storm would have been difficult to defend against.
Aurelian simply raised his hand.
Heavenly Luminance divine light spread outward.
The black blade fragments melted like snow beneath the sun.

Corvin tried to charge through the light with his armor glowing, but Aurelian’s expression remained calm. A golden-white spear of light appeared above him and descended. It broke Corvin’s armor, forced him to one knee, and stopped just above his head.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Corvin Nightsteel Eliminated.]
Max’s gaze became cold.

Aurelian still had not shown the full depth of the bloodline he had received, but every time he used that light, Max could feel the connection more clearly. It was like watching someone use a stolen part of his own existence.
Selene Vaeloria’s battle came later.
[Second Main Round, Battle Fifteen]
[Selene Vaeloria vs Aurelia Flamecrest]

This pairing became one of the first battles in the second main round where a famous genius was given a truly troublesome opponent. Aurelia Flamecrest had advanced through a hard-fought match in the first main round and possessed extremely powerful sunfire. The moment the battle began, she released a golden sun wheel that pushed even Selene’s luminance aura back slightly.
Selene’s expression turned cold.

She raised both hands, and the Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar appeared faintly behind her. She did not use her Pseudo Cosmic Path, but the avatar alone increased the pressure of her light sharply. Aurelia’s sunfire clashed with Selene’s radiance again and again, and for the first time in this round, Selene was forced to take several steps back.
The crowd stirred.
"She is being pushed?"
"No, not pushed. She is measuring the attack."
Max watched calmly.
He could tell that Selene was not in real danger. Aurelia’s sunfire was strong, but Selene’s foundation was still higher.
As expected, after a few more exchanges, Selene’s gaze sharpened.
"Twelve Luminance Edicts."
Twelve golden runes appeared around Aurelia.
Her sunfire trembled.

The edicts suppressed the flames from twelve directions, and Selene’s palm descended immediately afterward. Aurelia tried to resist, but the radiant palm broke through her sunfire and stopped before her chest.
Aurelia clenched her teeth, then lowered her hands.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Selene Vaeloria.]
[Aurelia Flamecrest Eliminated.]
Selene returned to her pillar and looked at Max again, but Max’s expression remained indifferent.
Her hatred was obvious.
Her strength was real.
But Max had already defeated her once when she used far more than this.

The battles continued one after another. Some of the hidden experts who had looked promising in the first main round fell quickly when matched against more famous figures. Some managed to struggle, forcing their opponents to reveal a little more of their foundation before losing. The second main round was doing exactly what it was meant to do. It was separating the strong from the truly dangerous.
Revona’s second battle appeared near the later half.
[Second Main Round, Battle Eighteen]
[Revona vs Seraphine Lareth]
The moment the names appeared together, the arena became extremely quiet.
Seraphine’s face turned ugly.

She had survived the first main round, but now she had drawn Revona. Her Radiant Judgment Path was powerful, but after everyone had seen Revona’s Void Origin Eyes, no one knew whether Seraphine’s judgment light could even reach her.
Seraphine entered the stage with a cold expression.
Revona appeared opposite her with her eyes closed.
[Battle Begins.]
Seraphine attacked immediately.
Golden judgment spears descended from above, filling the stage with radiant killing light. Revona opened her eyes, and the void-colored glow appeared again.
The first spear vanished.
Then the second.
Then all the spears within her gaze disappeared one after another.
Seraphine’s expression became stiff. She clenched her teeth and released a stronger radiant wheel, trying to suppress Revona from above. But Revona looked up, and the center of the wheel was erased.
The entire technique collapsed.
Revona appeared before Seraphine and raised one finger toward her forehead.
Seraphine trembled with anger, but she could not deny the result.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Revona.]
[Seraphine Lareth Eliminated.]
Max smiled faintly.
Watching Seraphine lose so quickly was not unpleasant.

Fin Arclight’s battle came soon after, and unlike Seraphine, he managed to draw an opponent who was not a top monster. His Pale Eclipse Path dimmed the battlefield, weakened his opponent’s senses, and trapped them in a gray-white domain of distorted perception. After a short struggle, his opponent surrendered.
[Winner: Fin Arclight.]
Max watched Fin quietly.

Fin was not at the level of Damian, Rakan, or the others, but he remained troublesome. His Pale Eclipse Path was suited for weakening and trapping opponents, and if someone underestimated him, they could be dragged into a bad rhythm.
Morgana’s next battle also drew attention.
[Second Main Round, Battle Twenty-Two]
[Morgana Starveil vs Rose Valen]
Rose’s expression changed the moment her name appeared opposite Morgana’s.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
This was a bad match for Rose.

Rose was clever, careful, and skilled at creating traps, but Morgana was a witch whose curse methods specialized in turning other people’s preparations against them. If Rose tried to play a long tactical battle, she might end up giving Morgana more mediums to curse.

Corvin tried to charge through the light with his armor glowing, but Aurelian’s expression remained calm.
A golden-white spear of light appeared above him and descended.
It broke Corvin’s armor, forced him to one knee, and stopped just above his head.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Corvin Nightsteel Eliminated.]
Max’s gaze became cold.
Aurelian still had not shown the full depth of the bloodline he had received, but every time he used that light, Max could feel the connection more clearly.
It was like watching someone use a stolen part of his own existence.
Selene Vaeloria’s battle came later.
[Second Main Round, Battle Fifteen]
[Selene Vaeloria vs Aurelia Flamecrest]
This pairing became one of the first battles in the second main round where a famous genius was given a truly troublesome opponent.
Aurelia Flamecrest had advanced through a hard-fought match in the first main round and possessed extremely powerful sunfire.
The moment the battle began, she released a golden sun wheel that pushed even Selene’s luminance aura back slightly.
Selene’s expression turned cold.
She raised both hands, and the Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar appeared faintly behind her.
She did not use her Pseudo Cosmic Path, but the avatar alone increased the pressure of her light sharply.
Aurelia’s sunfire clashed with Selene’s radiance again and again, and for the first time in this round, Selene was forced to take several steps back.
The crowd stirred.
"She is being pushed?"
"No, not pushed.
She is measuring the attack."
Max watched calmly.
He could tell that Selene was not in real danger.
Aurelia’s sunfire was strong, but Selene’s foundation was still higher.
As expected, after a few more exchanges, Selene’s gaze sharpened.
"Twelve Luminance Edicts."
Twelve golden runes appeared around Aurelia.
Her sunfire trembled.
The edicts suppressed the flames from twelve directions, and Selene’s palm descended immediately afterward.
Aurelia tried to resist, but the radiant palm broke through her sunfire and stopped before her chest.
Aurelia clenched her teeth, then lowered her hands.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Selene Vaeloria.]
[Aurelia Flamecrest Eliminated.]
Selene returned to her pillar and looked at Max again, but Max’s expression remained indifferent.
Her hatred was obvious.
Her strength was real.
But Max had already defeated her once when she used far more than this.
The battles continued one after another.
Some of the hidden experts who had looked promising in the first main round fell quickly when matched against more famous figures.
Some managed to struggle, forcing their opponents to reveal a little more of their foundation before losing.
The second main round was doing exactly what it was meant to do.
It was separating the strong from the truly dangerous.
Revona’s second battle appeared near the later half.
[Second Main Round, Battle Eighteen]
[Revona vs Seraphine Lareth]
The moment the names appeared together, the arena became extremely quiet.
Seraphine’s face turned ugly.
She had survived the first main round, but now she had drawn Revona.
Her Radiant Judgment Path was powerful, but after everyone had seen Revona’s Void Origin Eyes, no one knew whether Seraphine’s judgment light could even reach her.
Seraphine entered the stage with a cold expression.
Revona appeared opposite her with her eyes closed.
[Battle Begins.]
Seraphine attacked immediately.
Golden judgment spears descended from above, filling the stage with radiant killing light.
Revona opened her eyes, and the void-colored glow appeared again.
The first spear vanished.
Then the second.
Then all the spears within her gaze disappeared one after another.
Seraphine’s expression became stiff.
She clenched her teeth and released a stronger radiant wheel, trying to suppress Revona from above.
But Revona looked up, and the center of the wheel was erased.
The entire technique collapsed.
Revona appeared before Seraphine and raised one finger toward her forehead.
Seraphine trembled with anger, but she could not deny the result.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Revona.]
[Seraphine Lareth Eliminated.]
Max smiled faintly.
Watching Seraphine lose so quickly was not unpleasant.
Fin Arclight’s battle came soon after, and unlike Seraphine, he managed to draw an opponent who was not a top monster.
His Pale Eclipse Path dimmed the battlefield, weakened his opponent’s senses, and trapped them in a gray-white domain of distorted perception.
After a short struggle, his opponent surrendered.
[Winner: Fin Arclight.]
Max watched Fin quietly.
Fin was not at the level of Damian, Rakan, or the others, but he remained troublesome.
His Pale Eclipse Path was suited for weakening and trapping opponents, and if someone underestimated him, they could be dragged into a bad rhythm.
Morgana’s next battle also drew attention.
[Second Main Round, Battle Twenty-Two]
[Morgana Starveil vs Rose Valen]
Rose’s expression changed the moment her name appeared opposite Morgana’s.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
This was a bad match for Rose.
Rose was clever, careful, and skilled at creating traps, but Morgana was a witch whose curse methods specialized in turning other people’s preparations against them.
If Rose tried to play a long tactical battle, she might end up giving Morgana more mediums to curse.

chapters.title: Chapter 1828: Final Round Starts!
paragraphs: Rose entered the stage with a serious face.
Morgana smiled sweetly. "How unlucky. You seem like someone who likes planning."
Rose did not answer.

The battle began, and Rose immediately spread several rune marks across the stage through subtle movements. She tried to keep distance and use defensive formations to block Morgana’s curse threads. For a short time, it worked. Her runes lit up one after another, forming protective layers around her body.
Morgana looked amused.
"Not bad."
Then she raised one hand.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Curse of the Borrowed Mark."
Rose’s runes trembled.
Her expression changed.

The protective layers she had placed began twisting, and several rune marks turned purple-black. Rose immediately cut off her connection to them, but Morgana had already closed the distance with curse threads spreading around her fingers.
A purple star appeared behind Rose.
Rose stopped moving.
Morgana’s voice was gentle. "If this were a real fight outside the arena, your soul would already be marked."
Rose’s expression was bitter, but she still lowered her blade.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Morgana Starveil.]
[Rose Valen Eliminated.]
Max watched Rose disappear from the stage.

She had lost, but she had not performed badly. Against most opponents, her formations and careful thinking could have won. Against Morgana, however, her own preparation had become a weakness. The matchup had been too unfavorable.
Morgana returned to her pillar and glanced toward Max again.
This time, Max finally looked back at her directly.
Morgana’s smile paused slightly.

There was no killing intent in Max’s gaze, but the calmness in his eyes made her remember the sword that had split her in half near the Witch God Tree. Her smile returned quickly, but it was a little less relaxed than before.
The final few battles of the second main round passed quickly.

A silent swordsman from an unknown force defeated a beast prince in three sword moves, revealing enough skill to draw even Damian’s attention. A bloodfire woman from the Blood Sun Temple won after a brutal clash that left half the stage covered in crimson flames. A soul-bell user had already fallen to Max, making the remaining mind-path participants much more cautious whenever they looked at him. Several other participants advanced with difficulty, while others disappeared under beams of elimination light.
At last, the twenty-fifth battle ended.
The giant screen above the arena changed again.
[Second Main Round Completed.]
[Total Participants At Start Of Round: 50]
[Eliminated Participants: 25]
[Remaining Participants: 25]
The dimmed pillars of the eliminated participants sank into the darkness below.
Only twenty-five pillars remained around the central arena.
The space suddenly felt much emptier.
And much more oppressive.
Angelina Valerius looked across the remaining participants with a calm expression.
"Congratulations," she said. "You have entered the final competitive stage of the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
Max looked around and saw the top experts were looking at each other with caution in their eyes.
Along with them, several hidden experts with strange and dangerous methods had also survived. Rose had been eliminated, Seraphine had been eliminated, and many others who had seemed strong were gone.
From this point onward, there would be no more random elimination bracket.
Each of the remaining twenty-five would fight twenty-four battles.
Everyone would face everyone.
Max’s gaze swept across the final competitors, and his smile became faint.
Now, there was no need to wonder when he would meet Damian, Rakan, Orion, Kaiden, Ervin, Revona, Rosaline, Aurelian, Selene, Morgana, or anyone else.
He would fight them all.
Angelina raised her hand, and the arena lights became brighter.
"The final competitive stage will begin after a short preparation period."
The twenty-five remaining pillars hummed.
The true battle for the championship was finally about to begin.
The twenty-five remaining pillars shone brighter than before.

After the second main round ended, the arena inside the Eternal Hourglass had become much emptier, yet the pressure in the air had increased many times over. Only twenty-five participants remained, and every one of them had already proven that they were strong enough to survive two direct elimination rounds. The weak were gone. The lucky were gone.
The ones who remained were either monsters standing openly at the peak or hidden blades that had not yet fully revealed themselves.
After the little rest, Angelina Valerius appeared again and stood above the central stage, her silver-white robe fluttering gently as she looked at the twenty-five participants surrounding the arena.
"The final competitive stage will now begin," she said calmly.
The massive screen of light above the arena changed, and the names of all twenty-five remaining participants appeared in a large circle.
[Final Competitive Stage Initiated.]
[Remaining Participants: 25]
[Battle Format: Complete Round-Robin Combat.]
[Each Participant Will Fight Every Other Remaining Participant Once.]
[Total Battles Per Participant: 24.]
[Ranking Method: Total Number Of Wins.]
Angelina’s voice continued, clear and dignified.

"In this stage, there will be no random elimination. No participant will be removed after a single loss. Each of you will fight every other participant once, which means each of you will fight twenty-four battles in total."
The expressions of many participants became serious.

A single loss would no longer end everything immediately, but that did not make the round easier. In fact, it made it much harsher. No one could rely on lucky pairings anymore. If someone wanted to become champion, they would have to defeat almost everyone.
Angelina raised one finger.
"After each battle, the battle record of the participant will be updated. Your name, total battles fought, and total wins will be displayed for all to see."
The giant screen above the arena changed again.
[Battle Record Format:]
[Participant Name]
[Total Battles Fought:]
[Total Wins:]

Angelina continued, "If two or more participants have the same number of wins after all scheduled battles are completed, tiebreaker battles will be conducted between them. If a participant surrenders, the surrender will count as a loss. If a participant is judged unable to continue, the battle will end immediately. If a participant refuses to stop after the arena has declared the result, that participant will be punished by the laws of the Eternal Hourglass."
The central stage hummed as if confirming her words.

"No outside interference will be allowed. No one may leave their pillar unless called to battle. Recovery time will be granted according to the order of battles, but in the final competitive stage, endurance is also part of strength."

Her gaze swept across Damian Voss, Rakan Thorne, Orion Starfall, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Revona, Rosaline, Aurelian Lareth, Selene Vaeloria, Morgana Starveil, Max, and the other remaining participants.
"Now, the first battle of the final competitive stage will begin."
The screen of light above the arena flickered.
Two names appeared.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle One]
[Max Morgan vs Rosaline Lunara]
