chapters.title: Chapter 1829: Max vs Rosaline
paragraphs: The moment those two names appeared, the arena became lively.

Many participants turned toward Max’s pillar, then toward Rosaline’s pillar. Some were surprised. Some were excited. Some were already focusing with great attention, because this battle was not between an obvious top monster and an ordinary survivor. Rosaline was not weak. She had advanced through both elimination rounds without suffering any real damage, and her radiant suppression had already proven to be extremely clean and dangerous.
Max also looked toward Rosaline.
Rosaline met his gaze from her pillar, and a faint helpless smile appeared on her face.
"I did not expect my first battle to start with you," she said.
Max smiled faintly. "Neither did I."
Angelina raised her hand.
Two beams of light descended.

Max appeared on one side of the central stage. Opposite him, Rosaline appeared with her golden-pink hair moving gently behind her, her white and rose-gold gown shining faintly beneath the arena light. She looked elegant, calm, and noble, but the aura around her was already becoming sharper.
Rosaline looked at Max seriously.
"I have watched enough of your battles to understand one thing," she said. "Against you, holding back is meaningless."
Max raised an eyebrow. "Is that so?"

Rosaline nodded. "Yes. Your body is monstrous, your sword foundation is terrifying, your soul defense is abnormal, and you still have several powers you have not shown properly. If I try to test you slowly, I will lose before showing anything worthwhile."
Max smiled nodding his head. "That is a good judgment."
Rosaline’s expression became solemn.
"So I will use my full strength from the beginning."
The moment her words fell, the atmosphere around the stage changed.

Golden-pink light rose from Rosaline’s body, soft at first, then brighter and brighter until it became like the first dawn spreading over an endless kingdom. The air filled with a sacred fragrance, and petals of radiant light began to fall from the sky.

Each petal looked gentle, but Max could clearly sense that every one of them carried sealing power, purification power, and a strange suppressive authority that tried to calm, bind, and weaken everything it touched.
The participants on the pillars became serious.
Damian Voss narrowed his eyes slightly. "She is revealing it from the start."
Orion Starfall smiled with interest. "So that is her Pseudo Cosmic Path. It’s very strong."
Kaiden Voidmere watched quietly. "A path combining radiance, sovereignty, and binding law."
Ervin’s abyss-like gaze focused on Rosaline. "Not bad."
Rakan Thorne grinned. "Good. This is what the final stage should look like."

Rosaline raised both hands, and behind her, a vast illusory kingdom appeared. It was made of golden-pink light, filled with towering palaces, radiant walls, floating crowns, and countless blooming flowers.
Above that luminous kingdom hovered a great rose-gold throne, and from that throne descended a gentle yet absolute pressure.
Rosaline’s voice rang across the stage.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary."
The moment the name was spoken, the entire battlefield transformed.
The central stage was covered by golden-pink light. Radiant petals fell in endless layers, and wherever they landed, the laws of the arena seemed to soften under Rosaline’s will.

Max immediately felt a suppressive force surrounding him. It was not violent. It did not try to crush him directly. Instead, it tried to seal his movements, purify his energy, suppress his killing intent, and weaken the sharpness of Dragonheart before he even drew it.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
This Pseudo Cosmic Path was strong.
It was not the kind of path that destroyed everything with raw power. It was a sanctuary-type path that turned the battlefield itself into Rosaline’s domain.

Inside this Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, her light strengthened herself, weakened enemies, purified hostile energy, sealed movements, and restrained violent intent. Against most opponents, this path would make them feel as if they were fighting an entire sacred kingdom by themselves.
Rosaline lifted one hand.
"Dawn Edict, First Seal."
A rose-gold seal appeared above Max.
It descended instantly.

Max stepped aside, but the petals beneath his feet lit up and tried to bind his movement. The seal followed him, adjusting its position as if it had already locked onto his presence. At the same time, several radiant chains rose from the ground and wrapped toward his arms and legs.
Max raised his hand and shattered the first chain with physical strength.
However, the broken chain turned into petals and reformed again.
Rosaline’s voice remained calm. "Inside my sanctuary, brute force alone will not end the binding."
Max smiled faintly. "I noticed."
The seal descended again.
This time, Max drew Dragonheart.

A sharp sword light cut upward and split the seal in half, but the split halves dissolved into more radiant petals. Those petals surrounded Max from all directions, each one releasing soft light that tried to suppress his aura and dull his sword intent.
The crowd watched with widened eyes.
"Rosaline’s Pseudo Cosmic Path is this strong?"
"She is actually forcing Max to defend."
"It is not ordinary defense. Her path is suppressing him from every direction."
"Against most people, this would already be enough to decide the battle."
Rosaline did not stop.
"Dawn Edict, Second Seal."
"Dawn Edict, Third Seal."
"Dawn Edict, Fourth Seal."

Three more seals appeared around Max. One targeted his body, one targeted his energy, and one targeted his weapon. The three seals descended together, while the sanctuary behind Rosaline became brighter. The rose-gold throne released a majestic pressure, and for a moment, it looked as if Max had been surrounded by the laws of an entire sacred kingdom.
Max’s expression finally became more serious.

He could break the seals one by one with sword moves and raw strength, but that would drag the battle into Rosaline’s rhythm. Her path was designed to slow, seal, and suppress. The longer he stayed inside it without answering with an equal level of power, the more troublesome it would become.
"So this is your full strength," Max said.
Rosaline’s gaze remained steady. "Not everything. But enough to make you take me seriously."
Max smiled.
"You have."
The moment his words fell, the air around him changed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1830: First Win!
paragraphs: The lively golden-pink light surrounding him suddenly began to quiet down. The falling petals slowed. The radiant chains trembled. The seals descending toward him paused for a fraction of a breath as if something unseen had passed through the battlefield and cut away the emotions supporting their authority.
Dragonheart released a silent, cold aura.
Rosaline’s eyes sharpened.
Max did not use Divine King Punishment.
He did not use his dragon scales.
He did not use his Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.
Instead, he raised Dragonheart and released the path he had just refined inside the reward chamber.
"Emotion Severing Path."
The moment the words left his mouth, the golden-pink sanctuary trembled.

A dark-gray sword aura spread outward from Dragonheart. It was not flashy. It was not grand. It was not loud. But wherever it passed, the radiant petals stopped glowing. The chains lost their binding intent. The seals lost their sense of authority. Even the majestic pressure of the Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary seemed to grow still for a moment.
Rosaline’s expression changed.
Max stepped forward.
One slash.
The first seal was severed.
Not destroyed.
Severed.
Its connection to Rosaline’s sanctuary was cut, and the seal dissolved into powerless light.
Second slash.
The radiant chains surrounding Max lost the will to bind and collapsed.
Third slash.
The petals in front of him split apart, and a clear path opened through the Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary.
Rosaline immediately raised both hands.
"Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary, Royal Mandate of Purifying Light."

The rose-gold throne behind her shone brilliantly, and an enormous pillar of golden-pink light descended toward Max. This was not a simple attack. It carried purification, sealing, and sovereign suppression together. It tried to purify the hostility in Max’s sword, seal the movement of Dragonheart, and suppress the Emotion Severing Path itself beneath Rosaline’s mandate.
Max looked up calmly.
Dragonheart moved.

The chamber training with the first owner of the Emotion Severing Path flashed through his mind for a brief instant. He remembered the warning that this path was volatile. He remembered that uncontrolled severing could devour the user. He remembered that the blade had to remain in his hand, not his heart. He remembered every word of the first user of Emotion Severing Path.
His eyes became colder, but not empty.
Then he slashed.
The silent sword light rose.
The Royal Mandate of Purifying Light split apart from the center.
The purification was severed from its target.
The sealing power was severed from its authority.
The sovereign suppression was severed from the throne behind Rosaline.
The massive pillar collapsed into scattered golden-pink fragments.
The entire arena went silent.

Rosaline’s face turned slightly pale, but she did not give up. The Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary behind her shook as she gathered its remaining power into one final attack. The radiant kingdom compressed into a single rose-gold crown above her head, and countless petals fused into a long spear of dawn light.
"Final Dawn Edict, Sovereign Rose Spear."
The spear shot toward Max. It carried all the remaining pressure of the sanctuary.
Max stepped forward and raised Dragonheart with both hands.
"Good attack."
Then he cut down.
Emotion Severing Path descended in a single silent line.
The Sovereign Rose Spear split apart.
The crown above Rosaline shattered.
The illusory kingdom behind her dimmed and vanished like a dream at sunrise.

Before Rosaline could gather another defense, Max’s figure appeared in front of her. Dragonheart stopped a finger’s width away from her throat. The cold severing aura did not touch her, but she could feel that if Max moved even slightly, the battle would end completely.
Rosaline looked at the blade near her throat, then slowly lowered her hands.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result calmly.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Rosaline Lunara Defeated.]
The screen above the arena immediately changed.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 1]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rosaline Lunara]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 0]
The arena remained silent for several breaths before whispers began spreading from pillar to pillar.
"She used her Pseudo Cosmic Path from the beginning and still lost."
"Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary was terrifying. It suppressed the whole battlefield."
"But Max’s sword cut through it."
"That Emotion Severing Path is too strange. It did not just destroy her power. It cut the connection behind it."
Damian Voss looked at Max with sharp eyes, his grip tightening around his sword.
Orion Starfall’s smile deepened. "So he finally showed it properly."
Rakan Thorne laughed softly. "That sword path is nasty. I like it."
Kaiden Voidmere’s silver-gray eyes became thoughtful. "It severed the authority behind the sanctuary. Very strange, how did Max do it?"
Revona opened her eyes for a moment, and the void-colored light in her pupils flickered faintly.

Aurelian Lareth’s expression became cold when he saw Max defeat Rosaline’s light-based Pseudo Cosmic Path so cleanly. Selene Vaeloria also stared at him with a darker gaze, remembering very clearly how Max had used another path to crush her own strength before.
Morgana Starveil smiled faintly from her pillar, but this time, the smile carried more caution than amusement.
On the central stage, Rosaline looked at Max and sighed softly.
"I knew anything less than my full strength would be useless, but I still did not expect you to break my sanctuary that cleanly."
Max lowered Dragonheart.
"Your path is strong," he said calmly. "Against most people here, it would be very troublesome."
Rosaline smiled faintly. "But not against you."

Max did not deny it. If he had fought against her before the reward chamber then perhaps, her attacks might have pushed Max to use his other Pseudo Cosmic Paths but after he came out of the reward chamber, his Pseudo Cosmic Path of Emotion Severing Path was nearing perfection state.
Rosaline shook her head lightly, then the transfer light descended and returned her to her pillar.
Max also returned to his pillar a moment later.
The first battle of the final competitive stage had ended.
Max Morgan had started with one battle and one win.

chapters.title: Chapter 1831: Fin vs Serena
paragraphs: Angelina Valerius looked across the twenty-five pillars after Max and Rosaline returned to their places.

The first battle of the final competitive stage had already set a heavy tone. Rosaline had used her Pseudo Cosmic Path from the very beginning, yet Max had still broken through it with Emotion Severing Path and taken the first win.

Because of that, the remaining participants no longer looked at this round as a simple sequence of battles. If even the first match had reached the level of Pseudo Cosmic Paths, then the battles that followed would only become more intense.
Angelina raised her hand.
"The second battle of the final competitive stage will now begin."
The massive screen of light above the arena flickered, and two names appeared in bright golden text.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Two]
[Fin Arclight vs Seren Frostveil]
The moment the names appeared, the arena grew quiet again.

Fin Arclight was not considered one of the absolute peak monsters like Damian, Rakan, Orion, Kaiden, or Max, but everyone knew he was dangerous. His Pale Eclipse Path had already shown its ability to weaken perception, dull energy flow, and trap opponents inside a strange gray-white field where their senses could no longer be trusted.

Seren Frostveil was also not simple. She had reached the final twenty-five with her refined ice control and calm battle judgment. Her frost techniques were not the most explosive, but they were precise, layered, and extremely difficult to break once she gained control of the battlefield. Against a direct attacker, she could slowly freeze the rhythm of the fight until the opponent had nowhere left to move.
Angelina looked toward the two pillars.
"Fin Arclight. Seren Frostveil. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Fin appeared on one side of the central stage, dressed in pale robes with gray-white moonlight gathering around him. His expression was cold and faintly arrogant, but after everything that had happened with Max, his arrogance had become more restrained than before.

Seren appeared opposite him in a robe of pale-blue and white, her ice spear resting lightly in her hand. Frost mist gathered beneath her feet the moment she arrived, but it did not spread too far yet. She looked at Fin calmly, clearly understanding that this would not be an easy battle.
Fin smiled faintly. "You are unlucky."
Seren’s expression did not change. "People who say that usually want to hide their own uneasiness."
Fin’s smile faded slightly.
Angelina’s voice rang out.
[Battle Begins.]
Fin moved first.

Gray-white light spread from beneath his feet, forming a pale crescent moon behind him. The light did not rush toward Seren in a straight line. Instead, it spread through the arena like a quiet eclipse, dimming the brilliance of the stage and making the air feel colder and heavier.
"Pale Eclipse Field."
The moment the field expanded, Seren’s frost mist trembled.
Her eyes narrowed slightly.

Within the Pale Eclipse Field, her perception became distorted. The distance between her and Fin seemed to stretch and shrink at the same time. His figure flickered in and out of sight, sometimes appearing near, sometimes far, and sometimes as several overlapping shadows. Even the flow of her energy became slightly sluggish, as if her body had been placed under moonlight that weakened movement, senses, and reaction.
Fin raised one hand.
Several pale crescent blades appeared in the air and shot toward Seren from different directions.
Seren stepped back and spun her ice spear.

Frost walls rose around her, blocking the first wave of crescent blades, but the moment those blades touched the ice, they did not explode. They slipped through the surface like pale moonlight passing through thin clouds, cutting toward her body from behind the wall.
Seren’s eyes sharpened.
She tapped the ground with her spear.
"Ice Mirror Formation."

Several ice mirrors appeared around her and reflected her body in different positions. The crescent blades passed through one reflection after another, but they failed to strike her real body. Seren appeared on the left side of the stage and thrust her spear forward. A dragon of frost rushed toward Fin, freezing everything in its path.
Fin smiled coldly and stepped into the eclipse light.
His body blurred.
The frost dragon passed through him and struck only an afterimage.
From the pillars, several participants watched with serious eyes.
"This matchup is troublesome."
"Fin’s Pale Eclipse Field distorts perception, but Seren’s ice mirrors can create false positions too."
"They are both trying to make the other lose track of the real body."
Max stood on his pillar and watched calmly.

Fin’s path was indeed annoying. It was not overwhelming like Selene’s light or sharp like Damian’s sword, but it created uncertainty. In a fight, uncertainty was dangerous because even one wrong judgment could decide the result.
On the stage, Seren suddenly raised her spear high.

Frost energy erupted from beneath her feet and spread outward in circles, freezing the ground, the air, and even parts of the gray-white eclipse light. Fin’s expression changed slightly as his Pale Eclipse Field slowed down for the first time.
Seren spoke calmly.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Frozen World Stillness."
The entire arena seemed to drop into a frozen silence.

A vast icy world appeared behind Seren. There were endless frozen mountains, rivers locked beneath transparent ice, snowstorms suspended in midair, and a pale-blue moon hanging over a silent winter kingdom. This was not ordinary frost. It was a path that tried to freeze movement, energy, sound, and even the rhythm of thought.
The Pale Eclipse Field trembled under the pressure.
Fin’s eyes narrowed. "So you had hidden this much."
Seren did not answer.
She thrust her spear forward.
The frozen world behind her responded.

Cold silence spread across the stage, and Fin’s eclipse light slowed visibly. His afterimages became fewer, his crescent blades became duller, and the distorted space around him began to freeze into clear lines. For the first time, his real body was forced to reveal itself.
A wave of surprise moved through the pillars.
"She forced Fin out of hiding."
"Frozen World Stillness can freeze even the distortion inside his field."
"Seren is stronger than I thought."
Fin’s expression became ugly.
Then he smiled coldly.
"Fine. Since you are using yours, I will use mine properly too."
The pale crescent moon behind Fin darkened.

Gray-white light turned deeper, and the entire stage seemed to enter an eclipse where the moon devoured the sun. His aura spread outward sharply, and a strange pressure fell upon the frozen world behind Seren.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Pale Eclipse Burial."

chapters.title: Chapter 1832: A Hard Fought Win
paragraphs: The moment the name rang out, the field changed completely.

An enormous pale moon appeared above the arena, half-covered by a black shadow. Beneath that moon, everything seemed to lose color. The frozen mountains behind Seren dimmed. The suspended snowstorms turned gray. Even the pale-blue moon in her frozen world began to look as if it was being swallowed by an eclipse.
Fin raised his hand.
"Eclipse Burial Blade."
A long crescent blade descended from the darkened moon.
Seren’s expression became serious.
She lifted her spear and released a storm of frozen light. The frozen world behind her pushed back against the eclipse, and countless ice spears rose into the sky to meet the descending blade.
The two Pseudo Cosmic Paths collided.
This time, the central stage shook violently.

The arena barrier lit up, and the runes beneath the stage blazed brightly to contain the impact. Pale eclipse light and frozen stillness devoured each other in waves. Fin’s path tried to bury Seren’s frozen world in a lightless eclipse, while Seren’s path tried to freeze the eclipse itself and stop its descent.
For a while, neither side gained a clear advantage.
Then Fin suddenly vanished.
Seren’s eyes narrowed.
A pale eclipse mark appeared beneath her feet.

Her Frozen World Stillness instantly reacted, freezing the mark before it could fully activate, but Fin appeared behind her at that same moment. His hand held a thin crescent blade of pale light aimed at the back of her neck.
Seren turned quickly and raised her spear.
Clang!
The crescent blade struck the spear.
Fin pressed forward.

Seren retreated half a step, then released a burst of frozen silence from her body. Fin’s arm stiffened slightly, and Seren used that opening to counter with a thrust toward his chest. Fin avoided it narrowly, but frost still spread across his shoulder.
Both separated at the same time.
For the first time, both of them looked slightly exhausted.
Max watched the battle with interest.

Seren’s Pseudo Cosmic Path was stronger than he had expected. If she fought someone who relied heavily on speed, sound, or energy flow, Frozen World Stillness would be extremely troublesome. However, Fin’s Pale Eclipse Burial was also dangerous because it could distort, bury, and weaken a battlefield from the outside in.
On the stage, Fin’s expression became colder.
He lifted both hands.
The pale eclipse moon above him darkened further, and several burial blades formed around it.
Seren’s face turned pale, but she also raised her spear with both hands. The frozen world behind her compressed into a single massive ice spear, its surface covered in pale-blue runes of stillness.
Fin spoke first.
"Pale Eclipse Burial, Moonless Descent."
Seren answered at the same time.
"Frozen World Stillness, Eternal Ice Spear."
The two strongest attacks descended and rose at once.

The moonless eclipse light fell from above, while the eternal ice spear shot upward from below. When the two collided, the center of the arena was swallowed by gray-white and pale-blue light. The impact was not as destructive as Max and Rosaline’s clash, but it was more suffocating. One power tried to bury the world in a pale eclipse, while the other tried to freeze that burial forever.
The collision lasted several breaths.
Then a crack appeared in the Eternal Ice Spear.
Seren’s expression changed.
Fin gritted his teeth and poured more power into his attack.

The Moonless Descent pushed downward inch by inch, finally breaking the ice spear apart. However, the Frozen World Stillness did not disappear without effect. The broken ice released one final burst of stillness, freezing most of the eclipse light and weakening its force before it could fully descend.
Even so, enough of the attack remained.
The weakened Moonless Descent struck Seren’s defense and forced her to one knee.
Her ice spear cracked.
Fin landed several meters away, breathing heavily but still standing.
Angelina Valerius looked at Seren.
Seren tried to stand, but the pale eclipse mark on her body flickered, suppressing her energy flow. After a few breaths, she lowered her head and sighed softly.
"I surrender."
Angelina announced the result.
[Winner: Fin Arclight.]
[Seren Frostveil Defeated.]
The giant screen above the arena changed immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Fin Arclight]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 1]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Seren Frostveil]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 0]
The arena remained quiet for a moment before discussions began.
"That was close."
"Seren actually forced Fin to use his Pseudo Cosmic Path properly."
"She almost froze his eclipse."
"But Fin’s path still won in the end."
"Both of them are strong enough to threaten many people here."
Max watched Fin return to his pillar.

Fin looked tired, but his gaze still carried pride. Seren returned to her own pillar with a pale expression, clearly affected by the loss, but she had forced out Fin’s true path and shown that she belonged among the final twenty-five.
Max’s eyes remained thoughtful.
’Pale Eclipse Burial,’ he thought. ’It is stronger than the version he used before, but not impossible to break.’
His gaze shifted to Seren.
’Frozen World Stillness is also troublesome. If she gains momentum, even movement and energy flow can be slowed.’
The second battle had made one thing clear.
The final competitive stage would not only be about the absolute monsters at the top.
Even the participants who seemed slightly below them had Pseudo Cosmic Paths capable of forcing serious battles.
Angelina Valerius looked at the result of the second battle for a moment before raising her hand again.

The massive screen above the arena flickered, and the names of the remaining twenty-five participants began to rotate once more. After Max defeated Rosaline and Fin defeated Seren, the atmosphere had become even heavier.

Everyone had already understood that in this final competitive stage, even the early battles could force out Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and no one could assume that a famous name would win without paying any price.
Angelina’s calm voice spread across the arena.
"The third battle of the final competitive stage will now begin."
The rotating names slowed down.
Two names enlarged at the center of the screen.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Three]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Morgana Starveil]

Her Frozen World Stillness instantly reacted, freezing the mark before it could fully activate, but Fin appeared behind her at that same moment.
His hand held a thin crescent blade of pale light aimed at the back of her neck.
Seren turned quickly and raised her spear.
Clang!
The crescent blade struck the spear.
Fin pressed forward.
Seren retreated half a step, then released a burst of frozen silence from her body.
Fin’s arm stiffened slightly, and Seren used that opening to counter with a thrust toward his chest.
Fin avoided it narrowly, but frost still spread across his shoulder.
Both separated at the same time.
For the first time, both of them looked slightly exhausted.
Max watched the battle with interest.
Seren’s Pseudo Cosmic Path was stronger than he had expected.
If she fought someone who relied heavily on speed, sound, or energy flow, Frozen World Stillness would be extremely troublesome.
However, Fin’s Pale Eclipse Burial was also dangerous because it could distort, bury, and weaken a battlefield from the outside in.
On the stage, Fin’s expression became colder.
He lifted both hands.
The pale eclipse moon above him darkened further, and several burial blades formed around it.
Seren’s face turned pale, but she also raised her spear with both hands.
The frozen world behind her compressed into a single massive ice spear, its surface covered in pale-blue runes of stillness.
Fin spoke first.
"Pale Eclipse Burial, Moonless Descent."
Seren answered at the same time.
"Frozen World Stillness, Eternal Ice Spear."
The two strongest attacks descended and rose at once.
The moonless eclipse light fell from above, while the eternal ice spear shot upward from below.
When the two collided, the center of the arena was swallowed by gray-white and pale-blue light.
The impact was not as destructive as Max and Rosaline’s clash, but it was more suffocating.
One power tried to bury the world in a pale eclipse, while the other tried to freeze that burial forever.
The collision lasted several breaths.
Then a crack appeared in the Eternal Ice Spear.
Seren’s expression changed.
Fin gritted his teeth and poured more power into his attack.
The Moonless Descent pushed downward inch by inch, finally breaking the ice spear apart.
However, the Frozen World Stillness did not disappear without effect.
The broken ice released one final burst of stillness, freezing most of the eclipse light and weakening its force before it could fully descend.
Even so, enough of the attack remained.
The weakened Moonless Descent struck Seren’s defense and forced her to one knee.
Her ice spear cracked.
Fin landed several meters away, breathing heavily but still standing.
Angelina Valerius looked at Seren.
Seren tried to stand, but the pale eclipse mark on her body flickered, suppressing her energy flow.
After a few breaths, she lowered her head and sighed softly.
"I surrender."
Angelina announced the result.
[Winner: Fin Arclight.]
[Seren Frostveil Defeated.]
The giant screen above the arena changed immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Fin Arclight]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 1]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Seren Frostveil]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 0]
The arena remained quiet for a moment before discussions began.
"That was close."
"Seren actually forced Fin to use his Pseudo Cosmic Path properly."
"She almost froze his eclipse."
"But Fin’s path still won in the end."
"Both of them are strong enough to threaten many people here."
Max watched Fin return to his pillar.
Fin looked tired, but his gaze still carried pride.
Seren returned to her own pillar with a pale expression, clearly affected by the loss, but she had forced out Fin’s true path and shown that she belonged among the final twenty-five.
Max’s eyes remained thoughtful.
’Pale Eclipse Burial,’ he thought. ’It is stronger than the version he used before, but not impossible to break.’
His gaze shifted to Seren.
’Frozen World Stillness is also troublesome.
If she gains momentum, even movement and energy flow can be slowed.’
The second battle had made one thing clear.
The final competitive stage would not only be about the absolute monsters at the top.
Even the participants who seemed slightly below them had Pseudo Cosmic Paths capable of forcing serious battles.
Angelina Valerius looked at the result of the second battle for a moment before raising her hand again.
The massive screen above the arena flickered, and the names of the remaining twenty-five participants began to rotate once more.
After Max defeated Rosaline and Fin defeated Seren, the atmosphere had become even heavier.

Everyone had already understood that in this final competitive stage, even the early battles could force out Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and no one could assume that a famous name would win without paying any price.
Angelina’s calm voice spread across the arena.
"The third battle of the final competitive stage will now begin."
The rotating names slowed down.
Two names enlarged at the center of the screen.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Three]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Morgana Starveil]

chapters.title: Chapter 1833: Divine Son vs Witch
paragraphs: The moment those names appeared, the entire arena reacted.
Aurelian Lareth was the Divine Son of the second elven faction, the vessel who had received Max’s stolen Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline.

Morgana Starveil was the witch genius from Stellar Templar, a dangerous woman whose curses had already defeated multiple opponents in extremely strange ways. Both of them were important figures, and both had already been marked by Max in different ways.
Max’s gaze immediately turned cold when he saw Aurelian’s name.
Morgana’s smile, on the other hand, became faintly playful.
"How troublesome," she said softly from her pillar. "I thought I would get to play with someone easier first."
Aurelian looked at her from across the arena with calm golden eyes.
"You are not qualified to call this troublesome yet."
Morgana’s smile deepened, but there was a trace of danger in her eyes. "Divine Son of the second faction, you sound even more unpleasant than the rumors."
Angelina raised her hand.
"Aurelian Lareth. Morgana Starveil. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.

Aurelian appeared on one side of the central stage, his white-gold robes spotless, his long golden hair falling behind him, and a sacred radiance flowing faintly around his body. He did not immediately release overwhelming pressure, yet his presence was heavy enough to make many participants narrow their eyes.

Morgana appeared opposite him, wearing her black-violet dress and witch hat, her midnight-blue hair moving gently as purple-black starlight gathered around her fingers. Her expression still carried a smile, but her eyes had already become serious.
She knew very well that Aurelian was not an opponent she could play with casually.
Angelina’s voice rang out.
[Battle Begins.]
Morgana moved first.
She raised her hand, and seven purple-black stars appeared behind her. Threads of curse energy shot outward from those stars, spreading across the battlefield like a spiderweb woven from night.
At the same time, tiny witch symbols began appearing beneath Aurelian’s feet, each one trying to connect to his shadow, his breath, his spiritual energy, and even the rhythm of his heartbeat.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Sevenfold Curse Thread."
Aurelian did not move.
Golden-white light spread from his body.
The curse threads closest to him began to burn.
Morgana’s eyes narrowed slightly. "As expected, ordinary curses are useless against that light."
Aurelian raised his hand.
A beam of Heavenly Luminance light shot forward.

Morgana’s figure shattered like a reflection, and the real her appeared several dozen meters away. The shattered reflection turned into a curse mirror that absorbed part of the luminance beam and reflected it back in a twisted purple-black form.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Mirror Curse Reversal."
The cursed light flew back toward Aurelian.
Aurelian’s expression remained indifferent.
He lifted one finger, and the cursed light dissolved before reaching him.
"Small tricks."
Morgana laughed softly. "Small tricks can still kill arrogant men."
Her hands moved quickly.

More curse mirrors appeared in the air. Some reflected light. Some distorted distance. Some showed false versions of Aurelian standing in different positions. Purple-black star marks spread across the stage, and within a few breaths, the battlefield seemed to have become Morgana’s witchcraft field.
Aurelian finally took one step forward.
The divine light around him brightened.
Wherever he stepped, the curse symbols on the ground burned away.
Morgana’s smile faded slightly.
The spectators on the pillars watched closely.
"Morgana’s curses are being purified."
"That is not ordinary light. Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance power directly counters many curse techniques."
"But Morgana is not weak. She has not used her Pseudo Cosmic Path yet."
Max watched silently.
His gaze was fixed mostly on Aurelian.

Every time Aurelian used that golden-white light, Max could feel a faint reaction from his own Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. It was disgust. Rejection. A deep instinctive hatred toward something that should never have belonged to Aurelian in the first place.
Aurelian lifted his palm.
"Heavenly Luminance, Sacred Spear Rain."
Dozens of golden-white spears appeared above the stage and descended toward Morgana.
Morgana raised both hands.
"Stellar Witchcraft, Thousand Night Veil."

A curtain of black-violet stars unfolded around her. The luminance spears struck the veil, and each impact caused a burst of golden and purple light. For a few breaths, the veil held. Then cracks began appearing across it.
Morgana clicked her tongue.
"Fine. Since gentle methods will not work, let us be a little rude."
The air around her changed.

The purple-black stars behind her expanded into a vast starry sky. Countless witch symbols floated within that sky, forming a circle of curses around a dark moon. A cold and ancient aura spread from Morgana’s body, and several participants immediately felt uncomfortable, as if invisible fingers had brushed against their souls.
Morgana’s voice became soft and dangerous.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Star-Curse Labyrinth."
The moment the path appeared, the battlefield changed.

Aurelian was no longer standing on the central stage alone. Around him, countless starry corridors appeared, each one filled with curse mirrors, witch symbols, and dark moonlight. The space within the arena did not truly expand, but perception, direction, and causality inside the field became twisted. Every step could lead into a curse.
Every attack could be reflected. Every attempt to break through could become a medium for another spell.
Several participants became solemn.
Orion Starfall’s smile turned thoughtful. "That path is nasty."
Kaiden Voidmere said calmly, "It distorts direction through curse connection, not space alone."
Ervin’s eyes narrowed slightly. "If one loses the first rhythm, it becomes difficult to escape."
Rakan Thorne grinned. "So I just smash everything."
Damian Voss glanced at him. "If you smash the wrong mirror, you may curse yourself."
Rakan laughed. "Then I smash the curse too."
Inside the Star-Curse Labyrinth, Morgana’s voice echoed from every direction.
"Divine Son, let me see if your light can purify a path made of curses."
Hundreds of curse mirrors lit up.

From each mirror, a different attack shot toward Aurelian. Some were shadow blades. Some were curse needles. Some were reflected versions of his own luminance spears. Some were invisible threads aimed at his soul. Some tried to mark his bloodline directly.

chapters.title: Chapter 1834: Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion
paragraphs: Aurelian’s eyes became colder.
For the first time, his calm expression changed.
A golden-white crown slowly appeared above his head.
The moment the crown appeared, Max’s expression turned colder.
His bloodline reacted more strongly.

Aurelian raised his hand, and behind him, an enormous figure of divine radiance began to appear. It was not the same as Selene’s Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar. This one was more masculine, more domineering, and filled with a sacred authority that seemed to stand above all lesser light.
Aurelian spoke calmly.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion."
Golden-white light exploded outward.
The Star-Curse Labyrinth trembled violently.
A divine kingdom of light spread behind Aurelian, filled with radiant pillars, sacred halls, and a golden throne beneath an endless sun.

The power of this path was different from Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary. Rosaline’s path was gentle, sealing, purifying, and suppressive. Aurelian’s path was far more domineering. It did not only purify. It judged, claimed, and overruled.
The curse mirrors closest to Aurelian cracked.
Morgana’s expression became serious.
"Dominion-type Pseudo Cosmic Path."
Aurelian looked at her through the collapsing labyrinth.
"Your curses have no authority before my light."
He raised his hand.
"Divine Dominion, Luminance Decree."
A golden decree appeared above the stage.
The moment it opened, countless words of light descended like law.
The curse mirrors shattered one after another.
The starry corridors burned.
The dark moon in Morgana’s path dimmed slightly.
Morgana’s face turned pale, but she gritted her teeth and pressed both hands together.
"Star-Curse Labyrinth, Nameless Witch Burial."

All the remaining curse mirrors broke at once, and from their fragments emerged a giant black-violet witch coffin covered in star symbols. The coffin opened toward Aurelian, releasing a terrifying curse meant to bury his light, seal his body, and drag his soul into the labyrinth’s deepest layer.
Aurelian’s eyes flashed.
The golden crown above his head shone brighter.
"Divine Dominion, Sacred Sun Judgment."
The endless sun behind him released a pillar of light.
The pillar struck the witch coffin directly.

For several breaths, the coffin resisted. Curse symbols crawled across the light, trying to contaminate it, while sacred radiance burned them away layer by layer. The clash shook the central stage, forcing the arena barrier to flare brightly.
Then the coffin cracked.
Morgana’s eyes narrowed.

The Sacred Sun Judgment pierced through the coffin and stopped just before her chest. The remaining light did not touch her body, but its pressure alone forced her to stumble back, blood flowing from the corner of her lips.
Aurelian lowered his hand.
The Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion still shone behind him.
"Surrender."
Morgana stared at him for a few breaths.
Her smile returned slowly, though it looked colder than before.
"How boring. Light-type opponents really are the worst."
Aurelian’s expression remained calm. "You lost."
Morgana wiped the blood from her lips and lowered her hand.
"I surrender."
Angelina Valerius announced the result.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Morgana Starveil Defeated.]
The screen above the arena changed immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Aurelian Lareth]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 1]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Morgana Starveil]
[Total Battles Fought: 1]
[Total Wins: 0]
The arena remained quiet for a moment.

This battle had not been one-sided. Morgana’s Star-Curse Labyrinth had clearly forced Aurelian to reveal his own Pseudo Cosmic Path, and that alone proved her strength. However, Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion had suppressed her curse path with frightening authority.
On his pillar, Max watched Aurelian silently.
His gaze was colder than before.
’Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion,’ Max thought. ’So that is the Pseudo Cosmic Path he built using what was stolen from me.’
The feeling was different from Selene’s Heavenly Luminance Genesis. Selene’s path felt pure, noble, and deeply rooted in her own bloodline.

Aurelian’s path was powerful, but to Max, it felt wrong. It was as if a stolen seed had been forcefully grown into a divine tree, beautiful on the outside but carrying a scent that made his bloodline reject it instinctively.
Aurelian returned to his pillar.
Before the light around him faded, he looked at Max.
Their gazes met.
Aurelian smiled faintly.
Max did not smile back.

Morgana also returned to her pillar, her face slightly pale but her eyes still sharp. She looked annoyed rather than broken. Losing one battle in this round did not eliminate her, but it had forced her to expose far more than she wanted.
Orion Starfall glanced between Aurelian and Max, then smiled with interest.
"This final stage is getting better."
Damian Voss remained silent, but his eyes had become sharper.
Rakan Thorne laughed softly. "Good. That guy is worth punching."
Kaiden Voidmere looked at Aurelian’s fading divine kingdom and said calmly, "That path is strong, but not flawless."
Revona’s eyes opened slightly, and the void-colored light in them flickered once before vanishing again.
After Aurelian Lareth and Morgana Starveil returned to their pillars, the weight of the final competitive stage became even clearer.

Three battles had already passed, and each of them had revealed something important. Max had defeated Rosaline’s Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary with Emotion Severing Path, Fin had barely overcome Seren’s Frozen World Stillness with his Pale Eclipse Burial, and Aurelian had suppressed Morgana’s Star-Curse Labyrinth with his Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion.

No one could call this stage ordinary anymore. Every participant among the final twenty-five carried enough strength to shock the outside world, but even among them, the distance between top geniuses and the rest was gradually becoming visible.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand again.
"The fourth battle of the final competitive stage will now begin."
The screen of light above the arena spun briefly before stopping.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Four]
[Damian Voss vs Corvin Nightsteel]
Corvin Nightsteel’s expression became extremely heavy the moment his name appeared opposite Damian’s.
When the battle began, Corvin immediately used his strongest defensive technique, causing countless black metal plates to overlap around him like a fortress.

Damian drew his sword once. A single sword light passed through the stage, and the black metal fortress split cleanly from top to bottom. Corvin froze in place, his heavy sword cut in half, while Damian’s blade stopped at his throat before he could launch his next attack.
Angelina announced the result without hesitation.
[Winner: Damian Voss.]
[Corvin Nightsteel Defeated.]

[Damian Voss]

[Total Wins: 1]

This battle would not be simple.

"Ervin. Selene Vaeloria. Enter the stage."

chapters.title: Chapter 1836: A Good Battle
paragraphs: Two beams of light descended at the same time.

Ervin appeared on one side of the central stage with his black spear resting lightly in his hand, his posture relaxed and his expression calm. He did not look excited, nervous, or arrogant. He simply stood there like a shadow beneath deep water, quiet enough to seem harmless at first glance, yet deep enough to make anyone with true perception feel uneasy.
Selene Vaeloria appeared opposite him.

Her white-gold hair fell behind her like a river of light, and her eyes carried the cold pride of the Divine Daughter of the second elven faction. Even after losing to Max near the Witch God Tree, she had not lost her confidence completely.

She was still Selene Vaeloria. She was still one of the most carefully raised geniuses of the second faction. Her Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline was pure, her foundation was terrifying, and her Pseudo Cosmic Path had already proven strong enough to force countless participants to lower their heads.
The moment she stepped onto the stage, the aura around her brightened.
Ervin looked at her quietly.
Selene also studied him for a few breaths.
"I know you are strong," she said coldly. "But I am not Morgana, and I am not one of those people you can defeat with one hidden spear thrust."
Ervin smiled faintly. "Good. Then this battle might be worth fighting."
Selene’s eyes narrowed.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand.
[Battle Begins.]
Selene attacked first.

Golden-white light burst from her body, forming dozens of radiant swords in the air. Each sword carried a trace of Heavenly Luminance power, sharp, pure, and oppressive. With a slight movement of her fingers, all the swords shot toward Ervin from different angles.
Ervin stepped forward.
His spear moved.

It was only a simple thrust, yet the spear tip seemed to pass through the gaps between the incoming radiant swords with impossible precision. One thrust broke three swords. A turn of the shaft deflected five more. A sweep of the spear scattered a dozen beams of light before they could reach him.
Selene’s expression did not change.
She raised her hand again.
"Luminance Sword Rain."

Hundreds of radiant swords appeared above the stage, far denser and more powerful than the first wave. They fell like a divine storm, covering every possible path of movement around Ervin. The attack was fast enough to make several participants narrow their eyes.
Ervin did not retreat.
He rotated his spear once, and dark energy spread from the spearhead in a thin circle.

The first wave of swords struck the circle and bent away slightly. The second wave pressed harder, forcing Ervin to finally move his feet. His body flickered through the sword rain, not with speed like Max’s Vein of Speed, nor with spatial distortion like Kaiden’s void movement, but with a strange sense of depth, as if he was stepping into shadows between moments.
He passed through the sword rain and arrived ten meters closer to Selene.
Selene’s eyes sharpened.
"Solar Luminance Palm."

A giant golden palm condensed in front of her and struck forward with majestic force. The palm carried heat, light, and suppressive pressure together, making the air tremble as it descended toward Ervin.
Ervin raised his spear with one hand.
A dark point appeared at the tip.
Then he thrust.

The spear tip pierced into the center of the golden palm. For a moment, the palm and spear stood in a deadlock. Then the darkness at the spear tip began spreading through the palm like ink dissolving inside clear water. The golden light dimmed from the center outward, and the entire palm collapsed before reaching him.
A murmur spread across the pillars.
"What kind of spear force is that?"
"It is not simple darkness."
"It devoured part of Selene’s luminance power."
Selene finally took one step forward.
The light behind her rose higher.
"Heavenly Wheel of Radiant Execution."

A massive golden wheel appeared above her, its edges covered in countless sharp rays of light. The wheel began rotating, and the sound of its movement filled the arena like divine law grinding against the world. Radiant pressure descended upon Ervin, trying to lock his body in place.
Ervin’s expression became slightly more serious.
The Heavenly Wheel shot forward.
He raised his spear horizontally and blocked.
Boom!
The impact forced him backward for the first time.

His feet slid across the stage, leaving two long marks on the dark-gold stone. The heavenly wheel pressed against his spear, spinning violently as sparks of golden light and dark energy exploded between them.
Selene’s eyes brightened.
She clenched her hand.

The heavenly wheel split into six smaller wheels, each one attacking Ervin from a different direction. This time, Ervin could no longer block them all with simple spear movement. His body blurred, his spear flickered, and several dark spear shadows appeared around him. The six wheels clashed with those spear shadows again and again, forcing him to retreat step by step.
On the pillars, Aurelian Lareth watched with a calm expression.
"She has improved her control," he said softly.
Max also watched carefully.

Selene was indeed strong. She had not used her Pseudo Cosmic Path yet, but her ordinary techniques were already enough to suppress most geniuses among the final twenty-five. If Ervin were an ordinary spear user, he would have already been cut apart by the heavenly wheels.
However, Ervin was not ordinary.
His spear suddenly changed.
The dark spear shadows around him stopped defending and turned into one straight line.
Ervin stepped forward instead of retreating.

His spear pierced through the gap between two wheels, then curved strangely and struck the inner edge of the third. The balance between the six heavenly wheels broke at once. The six wheels collided with each other in midair and exploded into golden fragments.
Selene’s gaze became colder.
"So you were waiting for the rhythm."
Ervin smiled faintly. "Your attacks are strong, but they still have structure."
Selene’s expression sank.
Behind her, a majestic female figure of divine radiance began to appear.
The pressure around the stage increased.
"Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar."

The radiant avatar rose behind Selene, noble and overwhelming, with a crown of light above its head and a spear of pure luminance in its hand. The moment it appeared, Selene’s aura rose sharply. The golden-white light around her became far more solid, and the pressure of her bloodline spread across the stage like a divine decree.

chapters.title: Chapter 1837: Abyssal Origin Descent!
paragraphs: Several participants became serious.
"She is using the Queen Avatar already."
"Against Max, she used this before going into her Pseudo Cosmic Path."
"This Ervin is forcing her faster than expected."
Selene lifted her hand.
The avatar behind her lifted its spear.
"Queen’s Divine Spear."
A spear of Heavenly Luminance shot toward Ervin.
This attack was different from the previous ones. It carried a noble, commanding force that tried to pierce through defense, energy, and will at the same time. Ervin’s eyes finally sharpened.
He held his black spear with both hands.
Darkness gathered around him.
Then he thrust forward.
The two spears collided.
The impact shook the arena barrier.

Ervin’s body trembled slightly, and the ground beneath his feet cracked. Selene’s light pressed forward fiercely, trying to overwhelm him with the purity of the Queen Avatar. The black spear in Ervin’s hand bent slightly under the pressure, but Ervin’s gaze remained calm.
A faint abyssal aura rose behind him.
It was not large.
It was not showy.
But the moment it appeared, Max’s Dimensional Sovereign Body sensed something strange.
Depth.
An almost impossible depth.

It felt as if there was something behind Ervin that did not belong to the surface of the world. Something deep beneath law, beneath space, beneath ordinary darkness. The abyssal aura did not roar or explode. It simply existed, and because it existed, the light of the Queen’s Divine Spear began to sink.
Selene’s expression changed.
Ervin took one step forward.
His spear pushed back the Queen’s Divine Spear.

Then he twisted his wrist, and the dark spear force spiraled into Selene’s attack, tearing open a narrow path through the luminance. He stepped through that path and appeared closer to Selene than before.
Selene immediately retreated.
At the same time, the Queen Avatar behind her raised its other hand.
"Twelve Luminance Edicts."
Twelve golden runes appeared around Ervin.
One sealed movement.
One suppressed energy.
One restrained weapon force.
One attacked spiritual will.
One weakened darkness.
One strengthened heavenly light.
The remaining six reinforced the first six, forming a complete suppression array around him.
For the first time, Ervin stopped.
The twelve edicts descended.

Selene did not wait. She joined both hands together, and the Queen Avatar behind her pointed its spear at Ervin once more. The pressure rising from her body made the entire stage glow with radiant lines.
Max watched without blinking.
’This is stronger than what she used earlier,’ he thought. ’She is not holding back.’
Ervin lowered his gaze slightly.
The twelve edicts pressed closer.
His black spear trembled.
Then he smiled.
"Not bad."
Selene’s expression became colder. "You still have time to surrender."
Ervin raised his head.
His eyes had changed.

They looked darker than before, not because of anger, but because something behind them had opened. The abyssal aura around him deepened rapidly, and the twelve luminance edicts surrounding him began to shake.
"I have not even truly started yet," he said.
The stage grew silent.
The darkness behind Ervin suddenly expanded.
It did not rush outward like a normal domain. It descended.
The air sank.
The light sank.
The sound sank.
Even the golden-white glow of Selene’s edicts seemed to become heavier, as if the entire battlefield had been placed above a bottomless sea and was slowly being pulled downward.
Ervin’s voice was calm.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Abyssal Origin Descent."
The moment those words appeared in the arena, almost every top genius reacted.
Damian Voss narrowed his eyes sharply.
Rakan Thorne stopped smiling.
Orion Starfall’s expression became truly serious for the first time.
Kaiden Voidmere’s silver-gray eyes flickered with a strange light.
Revona opened her Void Origin Eyes halfway.
Aurelian Lareth’s calm expression changed slightly.
Even Max’s gaze sharpened.
The Pseudo Cosmic Path behind Ervin was not an ordinary abyss path.

A vast black sea appeared behind him, but it was not made of water. It was made of depth, gravity, darkness, and some mysterious ancient origin that seemed to swallow the meaning of distance itself. Above that black sea stood a single broken gate, half-submerged, half-visible, covered in ancient symbols no one could clearly read. Behind the gate, there seemed to be something even deeper, but the arena laws prevented the vision from fully opening.
The twelve luminance edicts around Ervin sank at the same time.
Their light dimmed.
Their authority weakened.
It was not that they had been destroyed.
They had been dragged downward, buried beneath the pressure of the abyssal origin.
Selene’s face changed.
"Heavenly Luminance Genesis."
She did not hesitate anymore.
Her own Pseudo Cosmic Path erupted.

Golden-white light exploded from her body, and a pure world of first light appeared behind her. It was a world at the moment of creation, where dawn had just been born and all darkness was meant to be driven away. The Queen Avatar vanished, replaced by a higher and more ancient radiance. Her aura rose sharply, and the sinking feeling caused by Ervin’s Abyssal Origin Descent slowed for a moment.
"Pseudo Cosmic Path, Heavenly Luminance Genesis."
The stage became divided in two.
One side was an abyssal black sea with a broken ancient gate sinking into unknown depth.
The other was a world of first light, radiant and pure, as if heaven itself had opened at the beginning of creation.
The clash between them made the entire Eternal Hourglass arena tremble.
Selene raised her hand, her face pale but determined.
"Heavenly Luminance Genesis, Spear of First Dawn."
A spear of pure creation light condensed above her.
Max recognized it immediately.

This was the same kind of attack she had used before near the Witch God Tree, the attack that had forced him to take it with his dragon scales because Morgana’s roots had interfered. But now, Selene had poured even more hatred and pressure into it, and the spear seemed even more concentrated than before.
Ervin looked up at the spear.
For the first time, his smile disappeared.
He held his black spear tightly.
The broken gate behind him opened slightly.
A soundless pressure spread from inside the gate.
Max’s eyes narrowed.
’What is behind that gate?’
He could not see clearly.

Even his Dimensional Sovereign Body could only sense depth, danger, and something old enough to make ordinary perception feel useless. The Abyssal Origin Descent was not merely a path of darkness. It seemed connected to some origin beneath the world, a place where light, law, and matter all had to sink eventually.

chapters.title: Chapter 1838: Battle Continues one after another!
paragraphs: Ervin spoke softly.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Gate of the First Depth."
The broken gate behind him opened a little wider.
The black sea rose.
Selene’s Spear of First Dawn descended.
The spear and the abyssal gate collided.
There was no immediate explosion.

Instead, the golden-white spear pushed into the dark gate inch by inch, while the gate tried to swallow it into its depth. Radiance and abyssal pressure fought silently at first, then the entire collision erupted into a terrifying shockwave that struck the arena barrier from within.
Golden-white light tried to purify the abyss.
The abyss tried to drag the light downward.

Selene gritted her teeth, blood slowly flowing from the corner of her mouth. Her Heavenly Luminance Genesis burned brighter, but her energy was clearly being consumed at a terrifying speed. Ervin also did not look relaxed. His face was slightly paler, and the hand gripping his spear had tightened until his knuckles whitened.
For several breaths, the two seemed evenly matched.
Then Ervin took one step forward.
The black sea behind him rose again.
The gate opened another fraction.
The Spear of First Dawn trembled.
Selene’s pupils contracted.
The golden-white spear began to sink.
It was not breaking but sinking slowly by slowly.
The light was dragged into the gate, swallowed layer by layer by the Abyssal Origin Descent.

Selene forced out more power, and the Heavenly Luminance Genesis behind her blazed with desperate brilliance. For a moment, the spear shone brighter than ever before, piercing deeper into the gate and causing cracks to appear on its surface.
Ervin’s eyes darkened further.
"Abyssal Origin Descent, Return To Depth."
The black sea surged.
A terrifying pull erupted from the opened gate.
The cracked Spear of First Dawn lost its direction.
Its light curved.
Its radiance distorted.
Then, under the shocked gazes of the participants, Selene’s strongest attack was dragged into the gate and vanished.
The Heavenly Luminance Genesis behind her flickered violently.
Selene staggered.
Ervin did not give her time to recover.
He moved.

His figure crossed the stage in silence, not with speed but with depth, as if the distance between them had sunk beneath his feet. Selene tried to raise another luminance barrier, but the abyssal pressure around Ervin’s spear dragged the barrier downward before it could fully form.
His spear stopped in front of her chest.
The black spear tip did not touch her, but the abyssal aura around it made her entire body stiffen. Selene’s face was pale, and her Heavenly Luminance Genesis had already become unstable behind her.
Angelina Valerius looked at the stage calmly.
"Selene Vaeloria is unable to continue."
Selene clenched her teeth, humiliation and disbelief flashing in her eyes.
But she could not deny it.
She had lost.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Selene Vaeloria Defeated.]
The screen above the arena changed.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Ervin]
[Total Battles Fought: 3]
[Total Wins: 3]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Selene Vaeloria]
[Total Battles Fought: 3]
[Total Wins: 2]
The arena remained silent.
This silence was different from before.

When Max defeated Rosaline, everyone had been shocked by the strangeness of Emotion Severing Path. When Aurelian defeated Morgana, they had been shocked by the domineering authority of Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion. But Ervin’s Pseudo Cosmic Path had created a different kind of shock.
It was mysterious.
Heavy.
Deep.
It did not feel like an attack that simply destroyed its enemy. It felt like a path that returned everything to some unknown depth where all things eventually sank.
Rakan Thorne stared at Ervin with rare seriousness. "That guy is not simple."
Orion Starfall’s smile had disappeared. "Abyssal Origin Descent. I have never heard of such a Pseudo Cosmic Path."
Kaiden Voidmere’s eyes narrowed. "That gate is the problem. The sea is only the surface."
Revona looked at Ervin with her Void Origin Eyes open, and even she did not look completely relaxed.
Damian Voss’s grip tightened slightly around his sword hilt.

Aurelian Lareth’s expression became colder as he watched Selene lose. As the Divine Daughter of the second faction, Selene’s defeat was not merely personal. It also meant that the second faction’s prestige had been struck in front of everyone.
Max stood on his pillar, his gaze fixed on Ervin.
He had fought Ervin in the Genesis Trial. He knew Ervin was strong. He knew Ervin had hidden much of his power. But even Max had not expected his Pseudo Cosmic Path to be this strange.
’Abyssal Origin Descent,’ Max thought. ’That gate swallowed Selene’s Spear of First Dawn instead of breaking it. If I fight him, I cannot treat it like ordinary darkness or ordinary abyssal power.’
On the stage, Ervin withdrew his spear.
The black sea behind him faded slowly, and the broken gate disappeared last. Even as it vanished, Max felt as if something behind that gate had looked at the arena for a brief moment.
Selene was returned to her pillar by a beam of light, her face still pale and her eyes filled with unwillingness.
Ervin returned to his own pillar quietly, as if nothing special had happened.
But everyone now looked at him differently.
After Ervin returned to his pillar, the atmosphere inside the Eternal Hourglass remained heavy for a long time.
Selene Vaeloria had lost.

That fact alone was enough to silence many people. She was the Divine Daughter of the second elven faction, a wielder of the Heavenly Luminance Royal Bloodline, and someone who had revealed the terrifying Pseudo Cosmic Path, Heavenly Luminance Genesis.

Yet even after using the Spear of First Dawn, she had still been defeated by Ervin’s mysterious Abyssal Origin Descent. The black sea and broken gate behind Ervin had left a deep impression on every remaining participant, and even the top geniuses who had been relaxed earlier were now looking at him with more caution.
However, the final competitive stage did not stop because of anyone’s shock.
Angelina Valerius stood calmly above the arena and continued announcing battles.
The next few matches ended far more quickly.

A hidden swordsman from a minor divine force stepped onto the stage against a beast-blooded warrior and won in only four sword strikes, his blade moving so quietly that even some participants failed to catch the exact rhythm of his attack.

A bloodfire woman from the Blood Sun Temple defeated a soul-bell user by burning the sound waves before they could reach her mind, forcing him to surrender once his bells began cracking under her crimson flames.

Rosaline Lunara fought again and recovered from her earlier loss by suppressing her opponent with radiant seals, never needing to reveal Dawn Sovereign Sanctuary a second time. Fin Arclight defeated another mid-tier participant with Pale Eclipse Burial, though he only opened the edge of his Pseudo Cosmic Path for a breath before forcing his opponent to lose all sense of direction.

Morgana Starveil fought a silent spear genius and won by placing a curse on his shadow, causing every thrust he made to bend away from her at the last moment until he finally surrendered with an ugly expression.

Damian Voss met a powerful axe user whose battle intent was strong enough to make the arena floor crack, but Damian’s sword still cut through the axe, the armor, and the man’s fighting rhythm in one clean sequence.

Kaiden Voidmere faced a participant who used shadow movement, and the battle ended almost embarrassingly fast when Kaiden folded the path of the shadow itself and appeared beside him before the first assassination strike could land.

The battles continued, but for a while, the strongest names did not collide with one another.

It was not that the matches were boring. Every participant remaining in the top twenty-five was strong enough to dominate an ordinary generation. Even the ones who lost quickly still had methods that could make weaker geniuses despair.
But after Max against Rosaline, Aurelian against Morgana, and Ervin against Selene, everyone had already tasted the difference between a strong battle and a true clash of monsters.
Then Angelina raised her hand once more.
The screen above the arena began to rotate.
For some reason, the spinning names seemed slower this time.
The remaining participants looked upward.

Max stood calmly on his pillar, one hand resting near Dragonheart. Rakan Thorne stood on his own pillar, arms crossed over his chest, his wild grin already spreading as if he had sensed something before the names stopped.
The screen flashed.
Two names appeared.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Twenty-Three]
[Max Morgan vs Rakan Thorne]
For a breath, the entire Eternal Hourglass arena became silent.
Then the atmosphere exploded.
Rakan Thorne laughed loudly from his pillar, his voice rolling across the arena like thunder. "Finally!"
Max looked toward him with a faint smile.
The other top geniuses immediately focused.
This was different.
This was not a top genius fighting someone below the peak.
This was the first major collision between two true monsters of the final competitive stage.
And outside the Eternal Hourglass, the Divine Realm erupted.

Across countless cities, ancient forces, divine clans, floating palaces, hidden academies, merchant heavens, and starry viewing platforms, enormous light screens reflected the names of Max Morgan and Rakan Thorne.
The Cosmic Ascension Conference had already drawn the attention of the entire Divine Realm, but the moment this pairing appeared, countless spectators stood up at the same time.
"Max Morgan against Rakan Thorne!"
"The black dragon genius against the first Warlord of War God Palace!"
"This is the first real monster-level battle!"
"Max defeated Rosaline’s Pseudo Cosmic Path, but Rakan’s body is like a divine weapon. Can that sword path even cut him?"
"Rakan has not used his full strength once. He might be the strongest body-refining genius in the conference!"
At the Black Dragon Clan, the massive viewing plaza was completely packed.

Countless disciples stood beneath a gigantic screen suspended above the central square. On that screen, Max and Rakan’s names shone in golden light, and the moment the pairing appeared, the excitement that had filled the plaza turned into nervous silence.
Many young disciples clenched their fists. Some had been cheering loudly every time Max won, but now that his opponent was Rakan Thorne, their confidence was mixed with fear.
"That is Rakan Thorne..."
"The first Warlord of War God Palace."
"I heard he once crushed a divine mountain beast with his bare hands."
"He has not even been pushed properly until now."
"Max is strong, but Rakan is different. He is not someone you can defeat with ordinary methods."
"Stop saying unlucky things. Max already defeated Rosaline, and he has not shown everything either."
The disciples argued, but no one could hide the tension in their voices.
Rakan Thorne’s reputation was too heavy.

The War God Palace was one of the strongest first-rate forces in the Divine Realm, and its Warlords were not ordinary geniuses. Each Warlord represented battle, body, will, and war path taken to a frightening level. Rakan, as the first Warlord, carried a name that even other peak geniuses respected.

High above the plaza, Lady Virelia stood before the viewing screen, her elegant face calm but her eyes serious. Around her, the seven family heads of the Black Dragon Clan were also watching. None of them spoke for a while.
Then Lady Virelia softly said, "Max, do well."
Her voice was not loud, but the family heads beside her heard it clearly.

The Grimes family head Matthew nodded slowly. "This battle will show the Divine Realm whether his previous victories were only due to strange methods or whether he can truly stand against the strongest geniuses."
Lady Virelia did not turn away from the screen.
Her gaze remained fixed on Max’s figure.
"All the best, Max," she whispered.

The War God Palace disciples were roaring.

An enormous battlefield-like plaza shook beneath their voices. Thousands of disciples raised their fists, weapons, and war banners toward the huge screen above them. The moment Rakan Thorne’s name appeared opposite Max’s, the entire palace seemed to awaken with battle intent.
"Rakan!"
"First Warlord!"
"Crush him!"
"Show the Divine Realm the strength of the War God Palace!"
"Max Morgan is strong, but no one beats our first Warlord in close combat!"
"Rakan Thorne has not even used his War God Body yet!"
"Let that black dragon genius learn what true war power is!"
The disciples shouted until the sky above the War God Palace trembled.

Several elders watched from higher platforms, their expressions filled with pride and expectation. To them, Rakan Thorne was not merely a participant. He was one of the sharpest blades of their younger generation, a genius raised through blood, battle, pain, and endless war trials.
He was someone who could carry the War God Palace name into the next era.
In a shadowed corner above the battlefield plaza, a silent figure watched the screen.
Saint Reiner stood there without drawing attention.
His eyes were fixed not on Rakan, but on Max.

He had seen many geniuses. He had seen arrogant heirs, monstrous bloodlines, hidden physiques, and terrifying paths. But Max Morgan had become increasingly difficult to measure. Every time people believed they had seen his strength, he revealed another layer.
Saint Reiner’s gaze narrowed slightly.
"Boy," he muttered softly, "let me see your true strength now. Let me see my legacy shine once again."
Back inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan Thorne cracked his neck and stepped forward on his pillar.
"Max Morgan," he called out, his grin wild and excited. "I have been waiting for this."
Max looked at him calmly. "I know."

Rakan laughed. "You defeated Rosaline’s Pseudo Cosmic Path with that strange sword path. You crushed soul attacks like they were nothing. You have a strong body, a strong sword, and more secrets than anyone here. But against me, tricks will not be enough."

Rakan’s grin widened.
Angelina Valerius looked toward both of them.
"Max Morgan. Rakan Thorne. Enter the stage."
Two beams of light descended.
The Divine Realm held its breath.
The first major battle between the peak geniuses was about to begin.

chapters.title: Chapter 1840: To Not Use Dragonheart
paragraphs: Max materialized on one side of the arena, his white hair stirring gently in the breeze produced by the transfer. He stood in complete composure, his black clothing undisturbed and his expression at ease, while Dragonheart rested in his dimensional space without any hint that he intended to draw it.

Compared to the swelling clamor rising from the Divine Realm outside and the strained attention of every participant within the Eternal Hourglass, Max appeared almost unnaturally calm, as though this were not the first great collision between peak geniuses but simply another fight he had chosen to walk into on his own terms.
Rakan Thorne landed on the opposite side with far greater force.

The instant his feet met the ground, the dark gold stone beneath him shuddered. His tall and battle-worn frame seemed to carry the weight of an entire mountain shaped by war, and his bare arms bore faint bronze markings that resembled old scars earned through countless trials of tempering.
He carried no weapon, and he needed none. His fists served as his weapons, his body served as his armor, and the aura of war wrapped around him like an unseen beast waiting for permission to wake.
For several breaths, neither of them moved, and the entire arena seemed to hold its breath along with them.
Beyond the Eternal Hourglass, countless gazes across the Divine Realm were fixed on that same stage.
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples had stopped shouting altogether. They stared at the enormous screen with clenched fists, and many of them could barely remember to breathe.
At the War God Palace, the reaction was the exact opposite. The disciples roared louder with every passing moment until their voices shook the sky above the battlefield plaza.
"Rakan!"
"First Warlord!"
"Show him what true body strength means!"
"Crush the black dragon genius!"
At the center of the stage, Rakan studied Max for a long moment, and then his grin slowly widened.
"You are not drawing your sword?"
Max glanced down at Dragonheart and then looked back at Rakan. "Not for now."

Rakan raised an eyebrow. The excitement in his eyes deepened, though it now carried a trace of genuine surprise. "You used that strange sword path to defeat Rosaline. You carry the Sword of the Sword Sovereign. You traded pure sword techniques with Damian Voss and never once fell behind. And yet against me, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, you choose to not use your sword?"
Max smiled faintly. "That is right."
Rakan laughed, and the sound held no mockery yet. It was deep and rough and saturated with the desire for battle. "Do you understand what that means?"
Max regarded him calmly. "I do."
Rakan’s grin turned wilder. "Then tell me why."

Max lifted his hand and slowly closed it into a fist. A subtle ripple of physical force spread outward from his body. It was not energy, nor sword intent, nor the Pseudo Cosmic Path, but purely the strength of flesh contained beneath his skin, his bones, his blood, and a vitality that resembled that of a dragon.
The stage beneath his feet gave a low hum, as though the arena itself had recognized that the body standing upon it was far from ordinary.

"I have fought swordsmen, bloodline users, curse wielders, soul attackers, and cultivators of strange and unusual paths," Max said evenly. "But I have never properly measured my body against the strongest body cultivators in the Divine Realm."
His gaze settled on Rakan.
"And when people speak of body cultivation in the Divine Realm, they speak of the War God Palace."
The words carried clearly through the arena, and for a moment even the disciples of the War God Palace outside fell silent. Then the entire palace erupted with noise even greater than before.
"He wants to test his body against the War God Palace?"
"Against Rakan Thorne himself?"
"He is out of his mind!"
"Does he believe dragon blood alone can rival the first Warlord?"
At the Black Dragon Clan, many disciples looked stunned.
"He is really not using Dragonheart?"
"He intends to fight Rakan with his bare body?"
"That is far too dangerous. Rakan is no ordinary body cultivator."
Lady Virelia’s eyes narrowed slightly, and even the seven family heads grew solemn. They knew Max’s body was formidable, for they had witnessed enough to understand that much.
Even so, choosing to challenge Rakan Thorne in the very domain where Rakan was most terrifying remained an extraordinarily bold decision.
Matthew Grimes released a slow breath. "That boy truly refuses to walk any ordinary road."
Inside the arena, Rakan stared at Max for several long breaths before he smiled again. This time his smile carried more than excitement. It was nearly predatory.
"You have made an enormous mistake," Rakan said.
Max’s expression did not shift. "Have I?"

Rakan rolled his neck, and a series of loud cracks sounded from his bones. "If you had used your sword, your strange Cosmic Path, or any of your other hidden tricks, this battle might have grown complicated from the very first exchange. But if you wish to contend with me through the body alone, then you have walked straight into my kingdom."

A bronze aura rose slowly from Rakan’s skin, and the air around him grew heavy. His muscles did not swell in any exaggerated fashion, yet every line of his body seemed to become more solid, more ancient, and more oppressive.
The war markings along his arms brightened one after another, and thin cracks began spreading through the stage beneath his feet.
Rakan raised his fist.

"This body has been broken inside war furnaces, crushed beneath divine mountains, burned within battlefield suns, drowned in seas of blood, and rebuilt more times than I can count. Every bone in me has been tempered for combat. Every drop of blood in my veins carries the intent of war. Every breath I draw exists for the sake of battle."
His eyes locked onto Max.
"So allow me to teach you something, Max Morgan."
The bronze aura surrounding him grew suddenly denser.
"When you challenge the War God Palace in a contest of the body, you do not begin by testing us."
He took a single step forward, and the arena shook.
"You begin by surviving us."
