chapters.title: Chapter 1841: Going Head-to-Head with RAKAN!
paragraphs: Max looked at the cracks radiating outward from Rakan’s step, and the faint smile on his face never wavered. If anything, his eyes grew brighter with interest.
"Good," he said. "That is exactly what I wanted to hear."
Rakan’s grin froze for an instant before stretching even wider. "You truly are insane."

Max slowly raised both hands and loosened his shoulders. Dragonheart remained in its sheath. The Emotion Severing Path did not appear, nor did the Divine King Punishment, nor the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline. Not a single dragon scale covered his skin.
Only his body stood there, calm and prepared, and the sight alone made the blood of countless spectators run hot.
On the participant pillars, Damian Voss narrowed his eyes. "He genuinely intends to fight with his bare hands."
Orion Starfall smiled. "This is either arrogance or confidence."
Kaiden Voidmere replied evenly, "With Max, it may well be both."
Ervin kept his eyes fixed on the stage. "He wants to learn exactly where his body stands."
Revona glanced toward Rakan and then back toward Max. "That knowledge may cost him dearly."
Aurelian Lareth sneered faintly from his pillar. "Foolish."
Selene Vaeloria’s gaze turned cold. "He will suffer for that arrogance."
Morgana Starveil smiled with amusement, though her eyes were entirely serious. "Perhaps. But the people who dismiss him as merely arrogant usually live to regret it."
Angelina Valerius observed both fighters from her position above the stage. Her face remained composed, yet her eyes lingered on Max for a brief moment.

She had overseen countless battles, watched countless geniuses rise and fall, and judged countless varieties of pride. Some pride was hollow, and some pride was born of ignorance, but the pride Max carried resembled neither.
It felt like the pride of a man deliberately walking toward danger because he wanted to measure the height of the mountain with his own two hands.
Angelina raised her hand, and the arena barrier brightened.
[Battle Begins.]

Rakan’s grin vanished, and pure battle intent took its place. The first Warlord of the War God Palace sank slightly into his stance, drawing his fist back as the bronze aura around him condensed into a single terrifying point.
Max simply stood where he was with his body relaxed and his eyes calm.
Then Rakan moved.

The stage detonated beneath his feet, and his body shot forward like a bronze meteor, crossing the distance between them in a single instant. There was no elaborate movement technique behind it, no illusion, no distortion of any path, and no concealed trick.

It was raw physical speed born from a body refined to an abnormal degree. The air ahead of him compressed violently, and his fist ripped through it with a horrifying howl as it hurtled toward Max’s chest.
Max did not dodge. He stepped forward and threw a punch of his own.
Boom!

The two fists met head-on. A shockwave burst from the point of contact and swept across the central stage like an invisible storm. The dark gold stone beneath their feet fractured into circular patterns, and the transparent barrier enclosing the arena flared brightly as it absorbed the force rushing outward.
Something shifted in Rakan’s eyes. Max’s body had not been thrown backward, and his arm had not so much as trembled. He had taken Rakan’s punch directly and remained standing exactly where he was.
For a brief moment, the entire War God Palace grew quieter.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan’s grin slowly returned. "Interesting."
Max shook out his wrist once and smiled faintly. "Is that all you have?"

Rakan laughed, and in the next instant his body blurred again. This time he threw three punches in rapid succession. The first was aimed at Max’s shoulder, the second at his ribs, and the third at his jaw.

Each strike carried enough power to shatter a divine mountain, yet Max answered with movements just as direct. He blocked the first punch with his forearm, met the second with his elbow, and tilted his head past the third by the narrowest of margins before driving his knee toward Rakan’s abdomen.
Rakan dropped his arm and caught the knee.
Boom!

Another impact rocked the arena, and Rakan slid back half a step. It was only half a step, but it was enough. The eyes of every participant sharpened at once, because Rakan Thorne, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, had just been pushed backward in a purely physical exchange.

Rakan glanced down at the faint mark his foot had carved into the stage, then looked back up at Max. His smile stretched far wider than before, and the battle intent in his eyes sank to a deeper level.
"You really do have the body to back up those words."
Max lowered his leg without hurry. "I told you. I wanted to test it."
Rakan’s shoulders shook with laughter. "Good. Very good. Most people who claim they want to test their bodies against mine are already sprawled on the ground after the first punch."
He charged forward again, and the two of them collided at the center of the stage.

This time they did not trade only one or two blows. Their fists, elbows, knees, shoulders, and palms crashed together in relentless succession, and every collision produced a dull peal of thunder that made the stage tremble.

Rakan’s attacks were savage and wild, yet never careless. Every punch carried years of battlefield refinement, every step cut off one of Max’s possible retreats, and every roll of his shoulders concealed the seed of another strike.

Max answered with nothing but physical skill. His punches were direct, his footwork was stable, and his reactions were frighteningly sharp. Rakan’s blows fell like war hammers, but Max either met them head-on or shifted just enough to let their force slide harmlessly past before striking back.
His body lacked the visible oppressiveness of Rakan’s, yet the strength packed inside it was compact and dense and absurdly steady.
Boom!

Rakan’s fist hammered into Max’s forearm. Max rotated his wrist and drove a punch into Rakan’s chest. Rakan blocked it with his palm, but the force still bent his upper body slightly backward. Rakan surged forward and slammed his shoulder toward Max, and Max met him shoulder against shoulder.
The air between them burst apart, and both fighters took a single step back.
For the first time since the battle had begun, the grin on Rakan’s face dimmed, and he stared at Max with complete seriousness.
On the participant pillars, the reactions grew far more intense. Rakan was no longer playing around, and yet Max was still standing his ground.

Rakan laughed, and in the next instant his body blurred again.
This time he threw three punches in rapid succession.
The first was aimed at Max’s shoulder, the second at his ribs, and the third at his jaw.
Each strike carried enough power to shatter a divine mountain, yet Max answered with movements just as direct.
He blocked the first punch with his forearm, met the second with his elbow, and tilted his head past the third by the narrowest of margins before driving his knee toward Rakan’s abdomen.
Rakan dropped his arm and caught the knee.
Boom!
Another impact rocked the arena, and Rakan slid back half a step.
It was only half a step, but it was enough.
The eyes of every participant sharpened at once, because Rakan Thorne, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, had just been pushed backward in a purely physical exchange.
Rakan glanced down at the faint mark his foot had carved into the stage, then looked back up at Max.
His smile stretched far wider than before, and the battle intent in his eyes sank to a deeper level.
"You really do have the body to back up those words."
Max lowered his leg without hurry.
"I told you.
I wanted to test it."
Rakan’s shoulders shook with laughter.
"Good.
Very good.
Most people who claim they want to test their bodies against mine are already sprawled on the ground after the first punch."
He charged forward again, and the two of them collided at the center of the stage.
This time they did not trade only one or two blows.
Their fists, elbows, knees, shoulders, and palms crashed together in relentless succession, and every collision produced a dull peal of thunder that made the stage tremble.
Rakan’s attacks were savage and wild, yet never careless.
Every punch carried years of battlefield refinement, every step cut off one of Max’s possible retreats, and every roll of his shoulders concealed the seed of another strike.
Max answered with nothing but physical skill.
His punches were direct, his footwork was stable, and his reactions were frighteningly sharp.
Rakan’s blows fell like war hammers, but Max either met them head-on or shifted just enough to let their force slide harmlessly past before striking back.
His body lacked the visible oppressiveness of Rakan’s, yet the strength packed inside it was compact and dense and absurdly steady.
Boom!
Rakan’s fist hammered into Max’s forearm.
Max rotated his wrist and drove a punch into Rakan’s chest.
Rakan blocked it with his palm, but the force still bent his upper body slightly backward.
Rakan surged forward and slammed his shoulder toward Max, and Max met him shoulder against shoulder.
The air between them burst apart, and both fighters took a single step back.
For the first time since the battle had begun, the grin on Rakan’s face dimmed, and he stared at Max with complete seriousness.
On the participant pillars, the reactions grew far more intense.
Rakan was no longer playing around, and yet Max was still standing his ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 1842: War God Body!
paragraphs: Damian Voss narrowed his eyes. "His body is far stronger than I expected."
Orion Starfall’s smile grew brighter. "He really is fighting Rakan with nothing but his body."
Kaiden Voidmere watched with deep and thoughtful eyes. "There is no visible bloodline armor, no sword path, and no external force at work. What we are seeing is his base body."
Ervin kept his gaze fixed on Max. "That is no ordinary dragon physique. There is something else beneath it."
Revona’s eyes opened a fraction wider, and even she appeared somewhat surprised.

Aurelian Lareth’s expression turned colder, while Selene Vaeloria stared at Max with her hands clenched tight. Her earlier defeat at his hands suddenly felt even more humiliating than before. If Max’s body alone was enough to trade blows with Rakan like this, then how much had he truly held back during their battle near the Witch God Tree?
Outside the Eternal Hourglass, the viewing plaza of the Black Dragon Clan erupted.
"He took Rakan’s punch!"
"He did more than take it. He pushed Rakan back!"
"Max never even drew Dragonheart!"
"He is genuinely fighting the first Warlord with his body alone!"

Lady Virelia’s eyes gleamed faintly, and the seven family heads standing beside her looked far more animated than before. Matthew Grimes slowly curled his hand into a fist, unable to conceal the shock in his eyes.
"This boy," he muttered. "Just how many foundations is he hiding?"

At the War God Palace, the disciples no longer shouted so carelessly. They still believed in Rakan, but the easy confidence they had carried into the match had been shaken. Their first Warlord had failed to crush Max instantly, and that fact alone was enough to plant disbelief in many of their hearts.

On the central stage, Rakan drew a slow breath, looked at Max, and laughed once more. This laugh was different from the ones before it. It was not casual in the slightest, for it overflowed with genuine excitement.
"Max Morgan," Rakan said, his voice deep and resonant, "you are the first person in this entire conference who has made me happy in a contest of body against body."
Max smiled. "Then continue."
Rakan shook his head. "No. Not like this."
Max raised an eyebrow.

Rakan slowly lifted both arms and clenched his fists. The bronze markings running across his arms began to glow with growing intensity. At first they resembled old scars, but soon they took on the appearance of ancient runes seared directly into his flesh.
A crushing pressure radiated outward from his body, and the faint rhythm of a war drum seemed to echo from somewhere deep within his bones.
Outside the Eternal Hourglass, the disciples of the War God Palace shot to their feet.
"He is using it!"
"The War God Body!"
"The first limit! He is opening the first limit!"
"Rakan is finally taking him seriously!"

Across the Divine Realm, countless spectators snapped to attention. The War God Body stood among the greatest body cultivation inheritances of the War God Palace. It was said to contain seven limits, and each limit represented a shackle bound around the physical body.

For an ordinary body cultivator, breaking even the first limit was enough to transform them into a terrifying genius. Breaking the second could allow a cultivator to dominate an entire generation within the same realm, and breaking the third was a feat reserved for the true monsters of the War God Palace alone.
Rakan Thorne, the strongest inheritor of the War God Body in the current generation, had already broken three of those limits. Now he was opening the first.
A deep rumbling rose from Rakan’s body. It was not the sound of flowing energy. It was the sound of flesh, bones, blood, muscles, tendons, and organs awakening in unison.
"War God Body," Rakan said slowly.
The bronze light surrounding him erupted.
"First Limit. War Blood Awakening."
Boom!

The stage sank beneath him, and a terrifying wave of physical pressure swept outward like a storm. Rakan’s blood seemed to roar within his veins, and his skin gleamed with a bronze luster that made him resemble a living statue of war.
His muscles did not swell grotesquely, yet the density of his body had visibly changed, as though a single layer of the power sealed within every inch of his flesh had just been unlocked.

Max’s eyes sharpened. He could feel it with absolute clarity. Rakan’s strength had increased, and not by some slight or trivial margin. The instant the first limit opened, Rakan’s physical power had climbed to an entirely different level.
Rakan sank into his stance, and his grin returned.
"Now, Max Morgan, let us see how long that body of yours can keep up."
He vanished.
Max’s pupils contracted. Rakan reappeared directly in front of him and struck, and Max crossed both arms to block.
Boom!

The impact crashed into him like a divine mountain falling out of the sky. For the first time in the battle, Max was driven backward. His feet dragged across the dark gold stage and carved two deep trenches into it before he finally steadied himself.
The Divine Realm erupted once again. At the War God Palace, the disciples roared until the battlefield plaza itself seemed to shake.
"That is it!"
"The First Limit!"
"War Blood Awakening!"
"Crush him, Rakan!"
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples grew anxious once more, and their earlier excitement hardened into tense, clenched-jaw silence.
"He was pushed back."
"The first limit raised Rakan’s strength by too much."
"Can Max really keep this up without drawing Dragonheart?"
Lady Virelia watched in silence, but her eyes never strayed from Max for even a moment.
On the stage, Max lowered his arms. A faint red mark lingered on his forearms, and then it vanished almost as quickly as it had appeared. Rakan noticed, and his eyes lit up.
"Even that failed to injure you properly?"
Max rolled his shoulders and regarded Rakan with unmistakable interest. "That was better."
Rakan stared at him for a moment, and then he laughed louder than before. "Good. Then do not disappoint me too quickly."
Max smiled faintly and closed both fists. "I was about to say the same to you."
In the next instant, both of them moved, and the true battle of bodies finally began.

chapters.title: Chapter 1843: Releasing the First Vein
paragraphs: The moment they closed the distance, the central stage transformed into a battlefield of pure physical violence. Rakan’s body, empowered by the First Limit of the War God Body, no longer felt like mere flesh and blood. Every punch he threw carried the weight of a collapsing mountain, and every step he planted sent tremors through the stage.

The bronze light wrapped around him was not ordinary energy but the awakened force of his blood, his bones, his muscles, and his organs, all releasing the power that had been stored behind the first shackle of the War God Body.
He appeared before Max once more and drove a punch toward his chest. Max raised his arm and blocked it.
Boom!
The impact forced Max’s body to sink slightly. The dark gold stone fractured beneath his feet, and a ring of force rippled outward across the stage.

Before Max could answer with a counter, Rakan’s second punch had already arrived, followed by a knee strike, an elbow, and a crushing slam of his shoulder. His attacks chained together like the beating of war drums, and each one landed faster and heavier than the last.

Max blocked, deflected, and countered, yet the difference created by the first limit was impossible to ignore. War Blood Awakening had lifted Rakan’s physical power onto another plane entirely. His body had grown stronger, his blood burned fiercer, and every movement carried a violent rhythm of battle that sought to overwhelm Max completely.
Boom!
Rakan’s fist hammered into Max’s crossed arms again, and this time Max slid back several steps.
Outside the Eternal Hourglass, the War God Palace disciples roared with delight.
"Rakan is suppressing him!"
"Even Max Morgan cannot match the War God Body forever!"
"Crush him!"

At the Black Dragon Clan, many disciples ground their teeth. Max had not drawn Dragonheart, had not invoked the Emotion Severing Path, and had not even revealed his dragon scales. To them, the sight was equal parts thrilling and terrifying.

If Max could truly match Rakan through his body alone, his reputation would soar to new heights. But if he insisted on fighting this way for too long, he might suffer a crushing defeat before ever bringing out his real advantages.
On the stage, Rakan pressed the attack once more. His fist tore through the air and fell toward Max like a bronze war hammer.
Max raised his hand and caught it.
Boom!
The stage shuddered yet again. This time Max’s feet sank into the ground, but his body did not retreat a single inch.
Rakan’s eyes narrowed.

Max slowly lifted his head. There was no anger in his eyes, no panic, and no frustration. In their place shone a clear brightness, as though the pressure of Rakan’s War God Body had finally handed him the answer he had been searching for.
"You are strong," Max said.
Rakan grinned. "You are only realizing that now?"
Max shook his head lightly. "No. I confirmed it."
Rakan’s smile froze for the briefest moment.

Max released Rakan’s fist and stepped back once. His body grew utterly still. For an instant the sounds of battle seemed to fade around him, and even the violent bronze aura bearing down on him appeared to pause.
Then something deep inside Max’s body began to rumble. It started low, and it was deep and ancient, as though a sealed gate somewhere within him had begun to swing open.
The participants on the pillars sensed the change immediately.
Damian Voss’s gaze sharpened. Orion Starfall’s smile slowly dissolved into genuine focus. Kaiden Voidmere’s eyes narrowed as he murmured, "Something inside his body is awakening."
Ervin watched Max in silence, his abyssal gaze sinking even deeper. "Is one of his hidden foundations?"
Revona opened her eyes a little wider, and the void-colored light within them flickered as though straining to see through to the source of the change.
Aurelian Lareth frowned, and Selene Vaeloria’s face grew colder still.
Morgana Starveil tilted her head slightly, and for the first time in a long while her smile disappeared. "Now what is he opening?"
On the central stage, Max drew a slow breath as the rumbling within him grew louder. It was nothing like Rakan’s War God Body, in which blood and bones and muscles roared with the intent of war.

The change taking place in Max felt far more foundational and far more primal, as though the very root of his existence was being reinforced from within, and every part of his body was being reminded of its true origin.
A faint and profound glow surfaced beneath his skin. It did not resemble ordinary light in any way. It felt like the first pulse of life stirring inside an ancient body.
Max’s voice rang out with perfect calm.
"Seven Divine Veins."
Rakan’s eyes widened slightly as heard those words.
Max’s body rumbled once more, and this time the sound reached so deep that the stage itself seemed to answer it.
"First Vein."
The air around him sank.
"Vein of Origin."
Boom!

A terrifying pulse erupted from Max’s body. It lacked the wildness of Rakan’s War Blood Awakening, yet it ran far deeper. The instant the Vein of Origin opened, Max’s physical body seemed to grow heavier, denser, and more complete.

His bones, his blood, his muscles, his skin, his organs, and even the hidden foundation of his body were all strengthened at the root. This was no simple increase in raw strength. It was a reinforcement at the level of origin itself, as though his body had returned to a purer and mightier state of existence.
Cracks spread outward from beneath Max’s feet, but this time they were not the result of him being driven back. They came from the sheer pressure his body released while he simply stood in place.
The viewing plaza of the Black Dragon Clan fell utterly silent, and then someone shouted.
"What is that?"
"His body just changed!"
"He opened something inside himself!"
"Seven Divine Veins? Did he just say Seven Divine Veins?"

Lady Virelia’s eyes widened a fraction, and even the seven family heads looked shaken. Only a handful of people had ever known that Max cultivated the Seven Divine Veins, and since Lady Virelia was among them, her surprise was far milder than everyone else’s.

At the War God Palace, the shouting grew unsteady. The disciples who had been roaring for Rakan only a moment earlier now stared at Max in open disbelief. They could not comprehend what had just happened.

Max’s body had not swelled, he had not transformed into a dragon, and he wore no armor of any kind. Yet the pressure rolling off him made even some of the War God Palace’s own disciples feel their blood constrict.

chapters.title: Chapter 1844: Max Dominating The Battle!
paragraphs: On the stage, Rakan stared at Max, and then his grin returned fiercer than it had ever been.
"Seven Divine Veins.... Just how many secrets are you carrying?"
Max slowly closed his fist, and the air around his fingers compressed.
"I told you," Max said evenly. "I wanted to test my body. I never said I had shown all of it."
Rakan laughed loudly. "Good!"

He stepped forward. The War Blood Awakening within him roared back to life, and bronze light surged around his frame. He drew his fist back, gathered the full power of the First Limit, and punched with far greater force than anything he had thrown before.
Max punched as well, and their fists collided.
Boom!

This time, the outcome changed. Rakan’s arm trembled, and his bronze aura convulsed violently. The force of Max’s fist tore through Rakan’s arm, surged into his shoulder, and swept across his entire body. Rakan’s feet dragged backward over the stage, gouging two long trenches into the dark gold stone.
The entire arena froze. Rakan had been forced back, and it had been done with a fist. A pure and unadorned fist.
Max lowered his hand without a word. Rakan looked down at his own trembling arm, and for the first time in the battle, genuine surprise showed on his face.
Then Max moved.
He crossed the distance in a single step and drove a punch toward Rakan’s chest. Rakan crossed both arms to block.
Boom!

Rakan was shoved backward again, and Max pursued him instantly. One punch crashed against Rakan’s guard, another knocked his elbow aside, and a third landed squarely on his shoulder and tilted his entire body.

Rakan gritted his teeth and answered with a knee strike, but Max caught it with his palm. The impact unleashed another shockwave, yet Max’s arm did not so much as waver. He twisted at the waist and buried his own knee in Rakan’s abdomen.
Boom!
Rakan’s body folded slightly.
The disciples of the War God Palace stared at the screen in stunned silence.
"Impossible."
"Rakan is being pushed back?"
"That is the First Limit!"
"Who in the world can dominate the First Limit of the War God Body with pure physical strength?"
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the participants were no less shocked.
Damian Voss watched with narrowed eyes. "His physical foundation rose by far too much."
Orion Starfall spoke softly. "But how? Is the War God Body not the strongest body cultivation method in the world? How could Max surpass a War God Body?"

Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze remained deep and unreadable. "There is a legend about a technique called the Seven Divine Veins. It is said that by opening the seven divine veins hidden within one’s body, a cultivator could lay the foundation for the strongest physical body in the world. With the power it grants, one could supposedly shatter stars with nothing more than a flick of the fingers."
"What? How could a technique that powerful even exist?" Orion turned to stare at Kaiden in shock.

Even Damian was left speechless. Destroying stars with a mere flick of the fingers was godlike power even by the standards of the Divine Realm, and he simply could not understand how any single technique could grant a person that much strength.

Kaiden continued. "I heard from my master that no human has ever succeeded in opening all Seven Divine Veins. The difficulty of the technique is so extreme that even the Primordials only managed to reach the fourth vein. Because of that terrifying difficulty, the Seven Divine Veins technique was lost in ancient times, and I doubt even the Primordials ever possessed the complete version."
He looked toward Max and added, "As for how Max managed to open the first of the Seven Divine Veins, I have no idea at all."
Both Orion and Damian fell silent at his words. Neither of them had expected such a body cultivation method to exist, let alone one with a history like that behind it.
Aurelian Lareth’s expression darkened even further.

On the stage, Rakan finally steadied himself. A thin line of blood appeared at the corner of his mouth. He wiped it away with his thumb and studied the red stain for a moment. Then he smiled. It was not a casual smile, and it was not an arrogant one. It was a smile blazing with pure excitement.
"Max Morgan," Rakan said slowly, "you truly are worth fighting."
Max stood before him with the power of the Vein of Origin rumbling steadily through his body.
"Then fight properly."
Rakan laughed and charged forward again, but this time Max met him even more directly.

Their fists collided again and again, and every collision rang out like divine drums being struck above the world. Rakan’s War Blood Awakening granted him terrifying strength, but Max’s Vein of Origin had made his physical foundation absurdly stable.
No matter how ferocious Rakan’s attacks became, Max did not crumble, did not lose his balance, and did not give ground. Instead, he slowly began to seize control of the battle’s rhythm.

Rakan punched, and Max blocked before answering with a counter. Rakan kicked, and Max stepped inside the arc to strike his ribs. Rakan attempted a shoulder slam, and Max met the charge shoulder against shoulder and forced him back half a step.
The longer they fought, the clearer the truth became. With the First Vein open, Max was no longer merely matching Rakan’s First Limit. He was beginning to dominate it.
The Divine Realm was shaken to its core.
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples exploded into wild cheering.
"Max!"
"He is pushing Rakan back!"
"He is beating the First Limit of the War God Body!"
"Brother Max is insane!"
Lady Virelia finally allowed a faint smile to touch her face. The seven family heads exchanged glances, and the astonishment in their eyes was impossible to conceal.
Matthew Grimes exhaled slowly. "The Divine Realm will remember this battle."
At the War God Palace, the disciples grew tense, yet their fighting spirit refused to collapse. Instead, many of them began roaring once more, and this time their voices carried real urgency.
"Rakan!"
"Open the second limit!"
"Show him the true War God Body!"
"First Warlord, you cannot lose in a contest of body strength!"
In a shadowed corner, Saint Reiner watched the screen with narrowed eyes, and his entire attention rested on Max rather than Rakan.
Back inside the Eternal Hourglass, Max’s fist smashed through Rakan’s guard and struck him square in the chest.
Boom!
Rakan was hurled backward more than ten steps, and every step cracked the arena floor beneath him. He finally came to a stop, lowered his head, and released a long, deep breath.

The bronze light of the First Limit still burned around him, but the confidence in his eyes had transformed into something sharper. There was respect in his gaze now, along with excitement and an even fiercer hunger for battle.
Max stood across from him with the Vein of Origin still rumbling within his body, his expression calm and unshakable.
Rakan slowly raised his head.
"The First Limit is not enough," he said.
Max smiled faintly. "I noticed."
Rakan’s grin returned.
"Then let us go higher."

"Seven Divine Veins....
Just how many secrets are you carrying?"
Max slowly closed his fist, and the air around his fingers compressed.
"I told you," Max said evenly.
"I wanted to test my body.
I never said I had shown all of it."
Rakan laughed loudly.
"Good!"
He stepped forward.
The War Blood Awakening within him roared back to life, and bronze light surged around his frame.

Boom!

The entire arena froze.

Max lowered his hand without a word.
Rakan looked down at his own trembling arm, and for the first time in the battle, genuine surprise showed on his face.

He crossed the distance in a single step and drove a punch toward Rakan’s chest.
Rakan crossed both arms to block.
Boom!
Rakan was shoved backward again, and Max pursued him instantly.
One punch crashed against Rakan’s guard, another knocked his elbow aside, and a third landed squarely on his shoulder and tilted his entire body.

The impact unleashed another shockwave, yet Max’s arm did not so much as waver.
He twisted at the waist and buried his own knee in Rakan’s abdomen.
Boom!
Rakan’s body folded slightly.
The disciples of the War God Palace stared at the screen in stunned silence.
"Impossible."
"Rakan is being pushed back?"
"That is the First Limit!"
"Who in the world can dominate the First Limit of the War God Body with pure physical strength?"

Damian Voss watched with narrowed eyes.
"His physical foundation rose by far too much."
Orion Starfall spoke softly.
"But how?
Is the War God Body not the strongest body cultivation method in the world?
How could Max surpass a War God Body?"
Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze remained deep and unreadable.
"There is a legend about a technique called the Seven Divine Veins.
It is said that by opening the seven divine veins hidden within one’s body, a cultivator could lay the foundation for the strongest physical body in the world.
With the power it grants, one could supposedly shatter stars with nothing more than a flick of the fingers."
"What?
How could a technique that powerful even exist?" Orion turned to stare at Kaiden in shock.
Even Damian was left speechless.

Destroying stars with a mere flick of the fingers was godlike power even by the standards of the Divine Realm, and he simply could not understand how any single technique could grant a person that much strength.
Kaiden continued.
"I heard from my master that no human has ever succeeded in opening all Seven Divine Veins.
The difficulty of the technique is so extreme that even the Primordials only managed to reach the fourth vein.
Because of that terrifying difficulty, the Seven Divine Veins technique was lost in ancient times, and I doubt even the Primordials ever possessed the complete version."

chapters.title: Chapter 1845: Second Limit
paragraphs: Rakan’s words fell, and the entire central stage seemed to grow heavier under them.
The bronze light of the First Limit still burned across his body, but it was no longer enough, and everyone present could see that plainly.

The War Blood Awakening had allowed him to suppress Max for a brief stretch, but once Max opened the Vein of Origin, the rhythm of the battle changed completely. Rakan, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, had been forced back again and again in the very domain where he was supposed to reign supreme.

For the War God Palace, this was no small matter, and for the Divine Realm as a whole, it was even more shocking. Rakan Thorne was not merely a body cultivator. He was one of the most terrifying body cultivators of the entire younger generation, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, and a monster who had already broken three limits of the War God Body.

Yet Max, who belonged to no part of the War God Palace and had not even touched his dragon transformation, had dominated Rakan’s First Limit using nothing but the first vein of the Seven Divine Veins.

On the stage, Rakan lowered his head for a moment, and his shoulders began to shake. Then he started to laugh. The laughter began low, then swelled louder and louder until it rolled across the arena like thunder, saturated with excitement, madness, and burning war intent.
He slowly raised his head, and the casual confidence that had lived in his eyes was gone. In its place remained only the pure joy of finding an opponent capable of forcing him beyond his comfort.
"Max Morgan," Rakan said, his voice deep and rough, "you are dangerous."
Max regarded him calmly. "Is that a compliment?"

"It is the highest compliment I can offer you right now." Rakan clenched both fists, and the bronze markings across his body flared brighter. "The First Limit alone is enough to crush nearly anyone in this conference foolish enough to fight me body against body, yet you broke through it so easily."
Max said nothing, and Rakan’s grin stretched wider still.
"Good. Then I will not insult you by taking this slowly."

The moment those words rang out, the War God Palace disciples outside the Eternal Hourglass fell completely silent, for many of them knew exactly what was coming. At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples felt their throats tighten as well.

The enormous screen above the viewing plaza showed Rakan standing at the center of the stage with bronze light blazing around him like a war furnace, and every disciple could sense that the first Warlord was about to unleash a far more terrifying tier of physical power.

On the central stage, Rakan slowly spread both arms. The runes that had been glowing along his arms and shoulders began crawling across his chest, his back, his neck, and his legs. His skin took on a deeper bronze luster, and the sound rising from within his body changed in character. During the First Limit, his blood had roared like war drums. Now his bones began to answer.
Crack. Crack. Crack.
The sound was nothing like ordinary bones popping. It resembled divine metal being reforged inside a living body.
Rakan’s voice rang out.
"War God Body."
The pressure surrounding him climbed sharply.
"Second Limit."
The air around his frame twisted.
"War Bone Reforging."
Boom!

A terrifying wave of physical pressure detonated outward. The stage beneath Rakan’s feet sank several inches, and the cracks already webbing the dark gold stone tore wider. His body did not grow in size, yet his entire frame seemed to become indestructible.
The aura radiating from his bones grew so dense that even the geniuses watching from the pillars felt as though they were staring at a divine weapon shaped like a man.
The War God Palace erupted.
"The Second Limit!"
"War Bone Reforging!"
"Rakan has opened the Second Limit!"
"Now let us see how Max keeps up!"
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples clenched their fists once more.
"He went straight to the Second Limit."
"His body feels completely different now."
"Can Max’s Vein of Origin still dominate him?"

Lady Virelia watched without so much as blinking. The seven family heads beside her no longer spoke in casual tones, for all of them could tell that Rakan’s physical body had undergone a qualitative transformation.

The First Limit awakened the blood, and the Second Limit reforged the bones. With this limit open, Rakan’s body was not merely stronger. It had become harder to injure, harder to shake, and far more stable under any impact.
On the participant pillars, Damian Voss’s gaze turned grave.
Orion Starfall exhaled slowly. "This must be the true bodily foundation of the War God Palace."

Kaiden Voidmere gave a faint nod. "The First Limit released the power of his blood, and the Second Limit reinforces the body’s frame. If Max intends to overpower him now, pure strength will not be enough unless his own foundation runs even deeper."
Ervin watched in silence. "Rakan is not finished."

Just as Ervin spoke, Rakan raised his head once more, and the bronze light around him continued to climb. Max’s eyes sharpened slightly. Rakan had no intention of attacking with the Second Limit alone. He was still going.
The War God Palace disciples stared at the screen with widening eyes.
"He is not stopping?"
"Is he going to open the Third Limit as well?"
"Against Max, he is opening two limits back to back?"
Saint Reiner, standing in the shadows of the War God Palace, narrowed his eyes, and for the first time a faint trace of approval surfaced in his gaze as he watched Rakan.
"Good," he muttered. "Do not test him half-heartedly."

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan’s body rumbled yet again. This time the sound came neither from his blood nor from his bones, but from his flesh itself. His muscles tightened, his tendons gleamed, and every line of his body seemed to swell with explosive war power.

The bronze markings across his skin joined into a single unbroken pattern, forming an ancient design of war that covered him like living divine armor carved directly into his flesh. The pressure around him grew so heavy that the very space near his body appeared to tremble.

chapters.title: Chapter 1846: Third Limit
paragraphs: Rakan’s voice dropped deeper.
"Third Limit."
His eyes blazed with ferocious battle intent.
"War Flesh Unbound."
Boom!

The entire central stage convulsed. A pillar of bronze physical force surged up from Rakan’s body and slammed into the barrier above the arena, and the transparent dome flashed over and over as though battered by a storm of invisible fists.
Rakan’s flesh, bones, blood, tendons, organs, and muscles now resonated as one, producing a complete state of war embodiment that stood far beyond the First Limit.

The difference was immediate. If the First Limit had made Rakan feel like an awakened battlefield beast, and the Second Limit had made him feel like a divine weapon, then the Third Limit made him feel like a walking calamity of war.
Every breath he drew carried pressure, every heartbeat rang out like a war drum, and every twitch of his fingers forced the surrounding air to compress.
Across the Divine Realm, countless spectators rose to their feet.
"He opened the Third Limit!"
"The strongest disciple of the War God Body has revealed the Third Limit!"
"This is Rakan Thorne’s true physical strength!"
"Max pushed him this far!"

At the Black Dragon Clan, the earlier cheers died away once more. The disciples stared at the screen in a mixture of shock and worry, for the pressure pouring off Rakan was so terrifying that some of them felt their blood tremble even through the projection.
One disciple swallowed hard. "This is still just body strength?"
Another muttered, "How can a physical body alone release that much pressure?"
A third clenched his fists and said, "Max has to bring out more now. He cannot keep fighting with only one vein, can he?"
Lady Virelia’s eyes never left Max, and the seven family heads exchanged grave looks.
The first family head spoke slowly. "The Third Limit of the War God Body. This is no longer a simple enhancement."
The second family head nodded. "His blood, his bones, and his flesh have all been released. His body has entered a complete state of war."
The third family head looked at Max on the screen. "Now we will see whether Max can still suppress him."

On the stage, Max stood opposite Rakan with the Vein of Origin rumbling steadily inside him. The pressure of the Third Limit crashed toward him like a storm. His clothes whipped violently around him, his white hair streamed backward, and the ground beneath his feet cracked, yet his body did not bend.
Rakan slowly lowered his arms. His grin had vanished, and pure seriousness had taken its place.
"Max," he said, "from this point onward, if you insist on relying on only one Divine Vein, you might genuinely get hurt."
Max studied Rakan’s transformed state with calm eyes. He could feel the difference clearly. Rakan’s body had truly ascended to another level.

The First Limit had strengthened his blood, the Second Limit had reforged his bones, and the Third Limit had unbound his flesh. With all three combined, his physical body had become several times more terrifying than before, and this was no longer anything the First Limit alone could compare to.
Max smiled faintly. "Good."
Rakan’s eyes narrowed. "Still that same answer?"
Max clenched his fists, and the Vein of Origin within him rumbled at a deeper pitch. "Yes."
For a moment, the two of them stared at each other across the fractured battlefield. Then Rakan moved.

No one saw the first step clearly. The stage shattered beneath his foot, and his body materialized before Max like a bronze thunderbolt. His fist came down carrying no flashy display of energy but rather a bodily force so horrifying that the air ahead of it compressed into a visible wall.
Max crossed both arms, and Rakan’s fist landed.
Boom!
The impact was nothing like anything that had come before. Max’s body was blasted backward, and his feet tore across the stage, ripping open two deep trenches that stretched for dozens of meters.

The barrier behind him blazed with light, and only when he stomped down with tremendous force did his body finally come to a halt. The shock of that single stomp cracked the stage beneath him into a spiderweb pattern.
The War God Palace disciples exploded into cheers.
"The Third Limit!"
"That is the Third Limit!"
"Rakan is back!"
"Even Max cannot stand his ground against that!"
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples grew tense all over again.
But on the stage, Max slowly lowered his arms. His sleeves hung in tatters, and red marks streaked his forearms, yet his bones remained unbroken and his body had suffered no serious injury.
Rakan saw all of it clearly, and his eyes shone even brighter.
"You blocked that?"
Max flexed his fingers once, and the red marks along his arms began to fade. "That one was heavy."
Rakan laughed sharply. "Then take more!"

He appeared again. With the Third Limit open, his speed far exceeded anything he had shown before. The stage cracked with his every movement, and each punch carried a layered force born from his blood, his bones, and his flesh releasing their power in unison.

Max met him head-on, but this time every collision forced him to adjust his stance. The Vein of Origin kept his foundation remarkably stable, yet Rakan’s Third Limit now commanded enough raw force to shake even that stability.
Boom!

Fist met fist, and Max’s arm trembled slightly. Rakan followed with an elbow, and though Max blocked it, the impact drove his shoulder downward. Rakan spun into a kick, and Max caught the leg, but the sheer force shoved him sideways across the stage.

The rhythm of the battle had shifted once again. Rakan was no longer the one being dominated. With the Second and Third Limits open, he had dragged the fight back into balance, and in terms of pure explosive physical force, he had even begun to suppress Max once more.
The participants watched with burning focus.
Damian Voss spoke quietly. "Rakan’s body has become terrifying."
Orion Starfall nodded. "All three limits at once. No wonder the War God Palace is known as the strongest force in body cultivation."
Kaiden Voidmere looked toward Max. "And yet Max is still relying on only the first vein."
Ervin’s eyes remained calm. "This is still not his full physical strength."
Revona watched in silence while her Void Origin Eyes reflected both figures as they crashed together again and again.

The stage cracked with his every movement, and each punch carried a layered force born from his blood, his bones, and his flesh releasing their power in unison.
Max met him head-on, but this time every collision forced him to adjust his stance.
The Vein of Origin kept his foundation remarkably stable, yet Rakan’s Third Limit now commanded enough raw force to shake even that stability.
Boom!
Fist met fist, and Max’s arm trembled slightly.
Rakan followed with an elbow, and though Max blocked it, the impact drove his shoulder downward.
Rakan spun into a kick, and Max caught the leg, but the sheer force shoved him sideways across the stage.
The rhythm of the battle had shifted once again.
Rakan was no longer the one being dominated.
With the Second and Third Limits open, he had dragged the fight back into balance, and in terms of pure explosive physical force, he had even begun to suppress Max once more.
The participants watched with burning focus.
Damian Voss spoke quietly.
"Rakan’s body has become terrifying."
Orion Starfall nodded.
"All three limits at once.
No wonder the War God Palace is known as the strongest force in body cultivation."
Kaiden Voidmere looked toward Max.
"And yet Max is still relying on only the first vein."
Ervin’s eyes remained calm.
"This is still not his full physical strength."
Revona watched in silence while her Void Origin Eyes reflected both figures as they crashed together again and again.

chapters.title: Chapter 1847: Draconic Essences shock the world!
paragraphs: On the stage, Rakan’s fist hurtled toward Max’s head. Max ducked beneath it and drove a punch toward Rakan’s ribs, and Rakan took the blow directly.
Boom!

The force slammed into his body, but this time Rakan slid back only half a step. The Third Limit allowed his flesh to absorb and disperse the impact, while the Second Limit kept his frame perfectly stable.
Rakan grinned. "Your punch is still strong, but it is no longer enough."
Max regarded him calmly.
Rakan stepped forward again with his battle intent blazing even higher. "So, Max Morgan, will you open the second vein?"

Max did not answer right away. The Vein of Origin continued to rumble within him, steady and profound, but the pressure of Rakan’s Third Limit was now unmistakably pressing against its edge. Max looked at Rakan’s bronze war body and smiled faintly.
"You really are worthy of testing my body."
Rakan’s grin turned wild once more. "Then stop holding back."

The two of them rushed forward again. Their fists collided at the center of the stage, and the shockwave surged upward like a pillar of invisible force, rattling the barrier and making the entire Eternal Hourglass arena tremble. The battle had climbed to a new level.
For several breaths, Max and Rakan remained locked together at the center of the stage, fist against fist, body against body, and strength against strength. The whole arena shuddered beneath them.

The cracks running through the dark gold stage tore wider, and the ancient runes embedded in the arena floor glowed brighter, as though the Eternal Hourglass itself had been forced to reinforce the battlefield just to withstand their clash.

Rakan’s Third Limit burned at full power. War Blood Awakening roared through his veins, War Bone Reforging held his frame as steady as divine metal, and War Flesh Unbound released terrifying explosive power from every inch of his body.
In that moment, Rakan no longer resembled an ordinary young genius. He looked like a living weapon that the War God Palace had forged for the single purpose of crushing enemies with his bare hands.

Yet Max still stood before him. The Vein of Origin rumbled steadily inside his body, deep and ancient, strengthening his physical foundation at its very root. Even though Rakan’s Third Limit had dragged the battle back into balance and had even begun to suppress him in raw explosive force, Max’s eyes remained perfectly calm.
Rakan grinned fiercely. "Open the second vein."
Max looked at him, and the entire arena went quiet.

Countless spectators across the Divine Realm leaned forward without realizing they had moved. The disciples of the Black Dragon Clan sat rigid with tension, while the disciples of the War God Palace watched with burning eyes.

The top geniuses inside the Eternal Hourglass fixed their full attention on Max as well, because all of them understood what the second vein might mean. If the first vein alone had allowed Max to dominate Rakan’s First Limit, then the second vein would almost certainly lift his body to a far more terrifying height.
But Max only smiled faintly.
"I will not need the second vein against you."
The words fell like thunder, and for a moment even Rakan’s grin froze in place.
The War God Palace disciples erupted in fury.
"What did he just say?"
"He does not need the second vein against Rakan?"
"Arrogant!"
"That is the Third Limit of the War God Body!"
"Rakan, crush him!"

At the Black Dragon Clan, many disciples were stunned at first, and then their blood began to heat. They could not tell whether Max was being recklessly arrogant or whether he genuinely held another method in reserve, but they had already watched him produce miracles time and time again.
Lady Virelia’s eyes narrowed slightly, and the seven family heads stared at the screen without blinking.

Inside the Eternal Hourglass, Rakan slowly withdrew his fist and took a single step back. His bronze war body still radiated terrifying pressure, but his expression had grown deeper and far more serious.
"You will not need the second vein?" Rakan asked.
Max nodded calmly. "That is right."
Rakan stared at him for a moment and then laughed, and this time his laughter carried anger, excitement, and disbelief all at once.
"Good. Very good. Then show me what gives you the confidence to say that."

Max did not answer with words. Instead, something inside his body awakened. It was not another vein, nor a Pseudo Cosmic Path, nor Dragonheart, nor the Emotion Severing Path. Deep within his body, two thousand Draconic Essences stirred at the same instant.

The change was immediate. A low dragon’s roar seemed to echo from within Max’s flesh and bones. It did not leave his mouth, and it did not come from the outside world. It rose from inside his body itself, from the countless essences of dragon power that had been refined, accumulated, and stored within him over time.
The moment those two thousand Draconic Essences began to circulate, the Vein of Origin responded as though it had finally found the perfect foundation to strengthen.

The rumbling inside Max’s body grew heavier. His blood flowed like a hidden river of dragons, and his bones released a faint resonance of gold and black. His muscles tightened, though never in any exaggerated way. Instead, his entire body grew more compact, more refined, and more terrifyingly dense.
The profound glow of the Vein of Origin deepened, and within that glow, traces of dragon force flickered like ancient scales concealed just beneath the surface of his skin.
The aura around Max rose once, then twice, and then rose yet again.

The central stage began to sink beneath his feet. The air around his body compressed until faint ripples spread visibly outward. His white hair lifted slightly, and his eyes grew brighter, colder, and far more oppressive than before. He still had not transformed.
No dragon scales covered his skin, and no enormous dragon shadow loomed behind him. Yet everyone present could feel that his physical strength had entered an entirely new tier.
The participants on the pillars reacted at once.
Damian Voss’s eyes sharpened. "His body just rose again."
Orion Starfall’s smile disappeared completely. "That feels like dragon aura."
Kaiden Voidmere’s gaze grew immeasurably deep. "This must be the black dragon bloodline of the Black Dragon Clan."

Ervin watched in silence, though his expression grew more focused than before. "The Vein of Origin strengthens the root, and the dragon bloodline supplies overwhelming physical force. That combination is dangerous."
Aurelian Lareth’s face turned dark, while Selene Vaeloria stared at Max with clenched fists, her pride battered again and again by every new layer he revealed.

chapters.title: Chapter 1848: A Cheap Copy
paragraphs: On the stage, Rakan felt the change more keenly than anyone else. Max’s aura had risen, but Rakan was not convinced. Not yet. After all, an aura was only an aura, and body strength had to be proven through collision. The War God Body was not something that could be intimidated by pressure alone.
Rakan’s eyes blazed with war intent. "Then take this!"

He drew his fist back. The bronze markings across his entire body flared to life as the First Limit, the Second Limit, and the Third Limit resonated together. His blood roared, his bones hummed like divine metal, and his flesh poured out boundless war force.
The power of all three limits gathered into his right fist and twisted the air around it into a distorted vortex.
The War God Palace disciples roared along with him.
"Rakan!"
"First Warlord!"
"The Three-Limit War Fist!"
"Crush him!"
Rakan stepped forward and punched with everything he had. The stage shattered beneath him, and his fist tore through the air toward Max like a falling star of war.
Max raised his hand. He did not raise a fist, and he did not raise a palm. He extended a single index finger, calmly, and touched it to Rakan’s incoming fist.
Boom!

The impact detonated outward. The barrier around the central stage flashed violently, the arena floor beneath both fighters cracked in every direction, and a storm of compressed air swept across the stage with enough force that even the watching participants had to narrow their eyes.
But Max did not move. His finger remained pressed against Rakan’s fist, and Rakan’s full-strength punch had stopped dead.
The entire Eternal Hourglass arena plunged into absolute silence.

Rakan’s pupils contracted, and his body froze in place. The War God Palace disciples, who had been roaring only a moment earlier, suddenly lost their voices. Thousands of people stared at the giant screen as though their souls had drifted out of their bodies.

They had expected Max to block, or perhaps to retreat, and some had even expected him to reveal another vein. But not one of them had imagined he would stop Rakan’s full-strength Three-Limit War Fist with a single finger.
At the Black Dragon Clan, the disciples fell silent as well, and then the plaza exploded.
"One finger!"
"He blocked Rakan with one finger!"
"That was Rakan’s full-strength punch!"
"Max did not even move!"
"Brother Max is a monster!"

Lady Virelia’s lips parted slightly, and for one brief moment even she could not hide the shock in her eyes. The seven family heads stared at the screen while their expressions shifted again and again.
They had always known Max was special, and they had known he possessed hidden depths, but the scene before them had gone far beyond anything they had anticipated.
Inside the Eternal Hourglass, the top geniuses were shaken just as badly. Damian Voss’s hand tightened around the hilt of his sword. Orion Starfall stared at the stage and said nothing at all.
Kaiden Voidmere’s eyes reflected faint ripples of void, as though he were trying to perceive exactly how the Vein of Origin and the Draconic Essences had fused within Max’s body.

Ervin’s expression turned deadly serious, and Revona’s Void Origin Eyes stayed locked on Max’s finger. Aurelian Lareth’s face twisted into something ugly, and Selene Vaeloria went pale with disbelief.
Morgana Starveil whispered, "That is simply unreasonable."

On the stage, Max looked at Rakan with unshaken calm. Rakan’s fist trembled against his finger, and it was not because Max was pushing him back. It was because Rakan was still pouring his strength forward and could not move that one finger by even the smallest fraction.
Max spoke quietly. "Is this your full power?"
Rakan’s eyes went wide, and then he roared. He wrenched his fist back and punched again, and Max raised the same finger.
Boom!

The second punch stopped. Rakan attacked again with a third punch, then a fourth, and then a fifth. Each blow carried the terrifying strength of the Third Limit, each one shook the stage, and each one made the barrier flare, yet every single strike was halted by Max’s finger.
It happened again, and again, and again.

Rakan’s fists grew faster and heavier. His body blurred as he attacked from every conceivable angle, striking from the front, from the sides, from above, and from below. He threw straight punches, hook punches, elbow strikes, shoulder slams, and even a crushing knee strike that could have snapped an ordinary divine body in half.

Max never moved from his spot. Sometimes he used only the tip of his finger, sometimes he shifted it half an inch, and sometimes he turned his wrist by the slightest degree. But no matter how Rakan attacked, everything ended at that single finger.
Boom! Rakan’s fist slammed into Max’s finger and stopped.
Boom! His elbow crashed down and stopped.
Boom! His shoulder charge thundered forward and stopped.
Boom! His knee rose with enough force to split the stage in two, but Max’s finger pressed down lightly and pinned it in place.
The more Rakan attacked, the quieter the arena became. This was no longer a fierce exchange between equals. This had become a gap, and it was a visible and undeniable one.

Rakan, the man who had forced Max to reveal the Vein of Origin and then pressed him hard enough to call upon two thousand Draconic Essences, was now incapable of moving Max at all with his full power.

The shock in Rakan’s eyes deepened with every blocked strike. At first there had been excitement, and then disbelief, and then anger, and then raw unwillingness. But as punch after punch failed to budge Max’s finger, even that unwillingness slowly began to change into something else.
It became acceptance.

Rakan finally stopped attacking. He stood before Max, breathing hard, with bronze light still burning around him and his fists trembling from the repeated impacts. His body was not broken, and his will had not collapsed, but his eyes had changed completely.
He looked at Max’s finger, and then he looked at Max, and for a long time he said nothing at all.
The War God Palace disciples watched in silence. No one was shouting anymore.
Even Saint Reiner, standing in the shadows, remained quiet for several breaths. His eyes were fixed on Max, and the faint smile he had worn earlier had dissolved into deep contemplation.
"I expected this result," he sighed softly. "After all, the War God Body was never anything more than a cheap imitation of the Seven Divine Veins."

He alone understood the truth of it. In ancient times, no human had ever been able to use the Seven Divine Veins, and so a number of them had gathered together to create a crude imitation of the technique, which later came to be known as the War God Body.

From that point onward, the War God Body reigned as the strongest body cultivation art in existence, for the simple reason that no one alive could open even a single vein of the true Seven Divine Veins.

But Saint Reiner had always known that a cheap copy would forever remain a cheap copy. He had devoted himself to researching the Seven Divine Veins and had eventually managed to piece together the complete technique, along with the method for opening all seven veins.

Even so, not a single genius, nor anyone else from the War God Palace, had ever succeeded in opening the Seven Divine Veins, and it was this failure that had driven Saint Reiner to build the two combat towers in search of a successor worthy of inheriting his life’s work.

chapters.title: Chapter 1849: Rakan Admits Defeat!
paragraphs: Back inside the arena, Rakan slowly lowered his fists, and his bronze aura began to settle. Max watched him calmly and made no move to attack.
Rakan drew a deep breath, and then he laughed once. The laugh was not loud, and it was not arrogant. It was a rough sound woven from helplessness, admiration, and a warrior’s honest acceptance.
"I lose."

The words carried across the stage, and the entire Divine Realm fell silent once more. Rakan Thorne, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, had just admitted defeat in a battle of pure body strength.
Max lowered his hand. "You are strong," he said calmly.
Rakan looked at him and shook his head. "Not strong enough."
Max did not mock him.

Rakan stared down at his trembling fists and smiled bitterly. "I opened three limits of the War God Body, and I still could not move a single finger. If this had been a fight to the death, you would have crushed me the moment you brought out that dragon power."
Max remained silent. Rakan lifted his head again, and though his eyes still burned, the battle inside him had already ended.
"I accept defeat."
Angelina Valerius looked at the two of them and made the announcement in a calm voice.
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Rakan Thorne Defeated.]
The screen above the arena changed immediately.
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Max Morgan]
[Total Battles Fought: 2]
[Total Wins: 2]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 3]
[Total Wins: 2]
The result appeared before everyone, and for a moment no one reacted at all. Then the Divine Realm erupted.

At the Black Dragon Clan, countless disciples screamed Max’s name with everything their lungs could give, and some grew so excited that their voices cracked. Lady Virelia gazed at the screen with a faint smile, though her eyes held an emotion that ran far deeper than simple pride.
The seven family heads stood in silence for a few breaths until one of them finally burst out laughing, and soon the rest of them followed.

At the War God Palace, the disciples stayed quiet. No one blamed Rakan, and no one would have dared to. They had watched the entire battle unfold. Rakan had opened three limits and had fought with every ounce of power his body could release at this stage of his cultivation, yet Max had surpassed him in the very field that was the War God Palace’s greatest pride.
A defeat of that kind could not be waved away with excuses. It could only be swallowed.
On the central stage, Rakan looked at Max one final time as the transfer light began to descend.
"Next time," he said, "I will have broken the fourth limit."
Max smiled faintly. "We will see."
Rakan stared at him for a moment, and then he laughed loudly as the transfer light carried him back to his pillar.
Max returned to his own pillar a moment later, the Vein of Origin gradually quieting within his body while the power of the two thousand Draconic Essences settled back into his flesh.
The other participants looked at him differently now. Before this battle, they had known Max was dangerous. After this battle, they understood something far more unsettling.

Even when he set aside Dragonheart, the Emotion Severing Path, the Divine King Punishment, the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, his dragon scales, and every other hidden power he carried, his body alone was enough to crush one of the strongest body cultivators of the entire younger generation.
The final competitive stage had only just begun, but Max Morgan had already shaken the Divine Realm.
After Max and Rakan returned to their pillars, the entire Eternal Hourglass arena remained restless for a long while.

Rakan Thorne had lost, and he had not lost through swordsmanship, nor through a Pseudo Cosmic Path, nor through soul power, lightning, space, or bloodline suppression. He had lost in a battle of pure body strength, and that fact made the result far more shocking than any ordinary defeat.

The first Warlord of the War God Palace had opened the first three limits of the War God Body, yet Max had stopped his full-strength attacks with a single finger after combining the Vein of Origin with the power of two thousand Draconic Essences.
That one scene had swept across the Divine Realm like a thunderclap, and countless forces watching the conference quietly began recalculating Max Morgan’s position in their plans.

Inside the arena, the remaining participants also looked at Max with new eyes. Damian Voss’s gaze toward him had grown sharper, and Orion Starfall’s smile now carried a deeper layer of interest. Kaiden Voidmere watched him as though attempting to decipher a complicated secret, while Ervin remained silent, though his eyes no longer drifted away from Max casually.
Revona’s Void Origin Eyes opened and closed from time to time, as if even she was weighing how her nullification would fare against a body foundation of that kind.
Angelina Valerius did not allow the arena to linger in its shock for long, because the final competitive stage had to continue.
"The next battle will now begin," she said calmly.
The screen above the arena spun once more.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Twenty-Four]
[Selene Vaeloria vs Hadeon Granite]

Selene stepped onto the stage wearing a cold expression. She had already lost to Ervin, and that defeat plainly weighed on her pride. Hadeon Granite, by contrast, was a defensive fighter who had already endured several punishing matchups. The moment the battle began, he wrapped himself in layers of gray stone armor and tried to hold out while waiting for an opening.

Selene refused to give him one. Heavenly Luminance light flooded across the stage, and the Heavenly Luminance Queen Avatar materialized behind her in a flash. She raised one hand, and twelve radiant edicts descended at once. Hadeon’s stone armor cracked beneath the pressure and his barriers dimmed, and before he could reinforce them, a spear of golden white light came to a halt before his forehead.
"I surrender," Hadeon said bitterly.
[Winner: Selene Vaeloria.]

The next battle arrived quickly.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Twenty-Five]
[Damian Voss vs Yelric Flamehorn]

Yelric Flamehorn’s face went stiff the instant he saw Damian’s name. He had already lost to Revona, and now he faced the strongest genius of the Sword God Palace. Even so, he did not surrender on the spot, for his pride would not permit it. Flames erupted across his body, and he charged forward with a blazing halberd in hand.

Damian drew his sword. His first slash cut the flames apart, his second slash severed the halberd’s head from its shaft, and his third stroke of sword light came to rest at Yelric’s throat. The battle ended so cleanly that many spectators had barely begun to cheer before Angelina announced the result.

The battles pressed onward.

Rakan drew a deep breath, and then he laughed once.
The laugh was not loud, and it was not arrogant.
It was a rough sound woven from helplessness, admiration, and a warrior’s honest acceptance.
"I lose."
The words carried across the stage, and the entire Divine Realm fell silent once more.
Rakan Thorne, the first Warlord of the War God Palace, had just admitted defeat in a battle of pure body strength.
Max lowered his hand.
"You are strong," he said calmly.
Rakan looked at him and shook his head.
"Not strong enough."
Max did not mock him.
Rakan stared down at his trembling fists and smiled bitterly.
"I opened three limits of the War God Body, and I still could not move a single finger.
If this had been a fight to the death, you would have crushed me the moment you brought out that dragon power."
Max remained silent.
Rakan lifted his head again, and though his eyes still burned, the battle inside him had already ended.
"I accept defeat."
Angelina Valerius looked at the two of them and made the announcement in a calm voice.

paragraphs: [Final Competitive Stage, Battle Twenty-Six]
[Aurelian Lareth vs Vaela Sunspire]

Vaela Sunspire had already suffered one loss, yet she still unleashed the full measure of her sunfire the moment the battle began. Golden flames rolled across the stage and transformed half the arena into a burning solar field.

Against ordinary light cultivators, her sunfire might have posed a real problem, but Aurelian’s Heavenly Luminance Divine Dominion was simply too domineering. This time he did not even need to manifest it in full.

A golden decree appeared above the stage, and the sunfire was pressed down from on high as though a greater authority had descended upon it. Vaela struggled to resist, but Aurelian’s divine light pierced through her flames and stopped just before her chest.
She gritted her teeth and surrendered.
[Winner: Aurelian Lareth.]
[Vaela Sunspire Defeated.]

Max’s gaze turned cold once more as Aurelian returned to his pillar. Every time Aurelian wielded that divine light, the rejection stirring within Max’s bloodline grew clearer. The Divine Son’s strength was undeniably real, but to Max it still felt like a beautiful palace erected on stolen foundations.

The next several battles passed even faster. Kaiden Voidmere defeated a beast-blooded warrior by folding the space beneath his feet so that his charge collapsed halfway through. Morgana Starveil overcame a thunder-winged spearwoman by cursing the lightning around her wings until every burst of speed dragged the woman deeper into Morgana’s trap.

Rosaline Lunara faced a soul-path participant and calmly sealed his soul bells inside radiant petals, forcing his surrender before he could activate his strongest technique. Fin Arclight fought a bloodfire cultivator and scraped out a narrow victory after using Pale Eclipse Burial to dull the burning rhythm of the bloodfire, though the battle left him breathing harder than before.
The records kept shifting.

With every passing battle, the gap between the strongest participants and everyone else grew more obvious. The top geniuses kept on winning. Some claimed victory with casual ease, some prevailed only after drawing on a small portion of their deeper strength, and some concealed their trump cards so carefully that even their victories felt incomplete, as though everyone watching understood they had shown nothing but the surface.
Max fought again as well. His next opponent was a silver-haired beastkin genius named Kael Thornclaw, whose speed and claws had shredded several opponents earlier in the stage.

The moment the battle began, Kael underwent a partial transformation, silver fur sweeping down his arms while his claws gleamed like divine blades. He shot toward Max with enough speed to scatter afterimages across the stage.

Max did not call upon the Vein of Origin this time, because he did not need it. When Kael appeared behind him and slashed toward his neck, Max turned slightly, caught the incoming wrist, and hurled him across the stage. Kael twisted in midair, landed on his feet, and attacked again, but Max stepped forward and struck him once in the chest with his palm.
Boom!
Kael crashed into the barrier and slid down its surface, coughing blood. He tried to rise, and then he slowly lowered his head.
"I surrender."
[Winner: Max Morgan.]
[Kael Thornclaw Defeated.]

The result surprised no one anymore, yet it still thickened the pressure gathering around Max. After his victory over Rakan, even his effortless wins felt terrifying, because everyone understood that he was not using even a fraction of what he had revealed in that body battle.
Another battle followed.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Thirty-Two]
[Ervin vs Darius Stoneveil]
Darius Stoneveil entered the stage with several defensive layers already raised, but against Ervin, defense alone counted for very little.

Ervin’s black spear pierced through the barriers in a single unbroken line, not by shattering them with violence, but by sinking through them as though the distance between the spear and its target had simply been swallowed.
The spearpoint came to rest before Darius’s chest. Darius stared at Ervin with a pale face and surrendered without attempting to drag out the battle.
[Winner: Ervin.]
[Darius Stoneveil Defeated.]

[Ervin]

[Total Wins: 0]

Ervin returned to his pillar in silence. After his battle with Selene, no one regarded him as an unknown dark horse any longer, for his Abyssal Origin Descent had already placed him firmly among the most dangerous figures in the final stage.

Battle followed battle. Rakan also fought again after recovering from his loss to Max. His opponent was a sound-attribute participant who tried to attack his inner organs through vibration, but Rakan opened only the First Limit of the War God Body, crushed the sound waves beneath a roar of pure battle intent, and ended the fight with a single punch.
His victory restored a measure of morale to the War God Palace disciples, though the shadow of his defeat to Max still lingered over them.
[Winner: Rakan Thorne.]
[Battle Record Updated.]
[Rakan Thorne]
[Total Battles Fought: 4]
[Total Wins: 3]

The final competitive stage surged forward like a storm. Some participants began sinking under repeated losses, and others fought simply to keep their records even, but the top monsters continued their climb.

Max, Damian, Orion, Kaiden, Ervin, Revona, Aurelian, and a handful of others held their places near the front. Whenever one of their names appeared opposite a weaker opponent, the result felt almost predetermined, and the only real question was whether the weaker participant could force them to reveal anything useful before falling.

For a while, the strongest were never matched against one another, and that fact only wound the arena tighter. Every spin of the screen carried the same silent question. When would the next monster collide with another monster?
The answer arrived sooner than many had expected.
Angelina Valerius raised her hand once more, and the giant screen above the arena began to rotate.

Names flashed past one after another, including Max Morgan, Damian Voss, Aurelian Lareth, Kaiden Voidmere, Ervin, Rakan Thorne, Morgana Starveil, Selene Vaeloria, Rosaline Lunara, Revona, and Orion Starfall.
The light slowed, and the entire arena went quiet. Then two names expanded at the center of the screen.
[Final Competitive Stage, Battle Thirty-Nine]
[Orion Starfall vs Revona]

A wave of excitement rippled through the arena at once. Orion Starfall, the strongest genius of the Nine Star Court, had finally been matched against Revona, the woman whose Void Origin Eyes could nullify attacks and reduce even powerful techniques to nothingness.
Max’s eyes sharpened immediately, for this was a battle worth watching.
Orion looked toward Revona’s pillar and smiled faintly. "This will be troublesome."
Revona opened her eyes slowly, and the void-colored light within them flickered like some ancient emptiness given form.
"You think so?" she asked with a smile.
The arena fell completely silent.
Angelina Valerius looked toward the two of them and spoke calmly.
"Orion Starfall. Revona. Enter the stage."
